items.statement: No price escalation clause in contracts; delays beyond 5 months may trigger renegotiation

items.quote: The aluminium extrusion project at Kota is running as per schedule and phase one is slated to be commissioned by the end of next quarter.

items.statement: ECH plant two-thirds commissioned in October 2025, balance capacity expected by end of Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our ECH plant was commissioned in October '25 and the product has been well accepted in the market. We are in the process of commissioning the balance capacity and plant should stabilize in the current quarter.

items.statement: 68 MW green power project for Kota progressing as planned
items.quote: Our projects in aluminium chloride, calcium Chloride at Bharuch and the 68 -megawatt green power project for Kota, continue to progress as planned.

items.statement: Caustic soda volumes up 6% YoY on better capacity utilization
items.quote: Caustic soda volumes that were up 6%, on account of better capacity utilization.

items.statement: Hydrogen peroxide plant running at close to capacity but industry oversupplied
items.quote: Currently, our plant itself is running at close to capacity. As an industry in India, it is an oversupply scenario at this point.

items.statement: Caustic soda demand robust domestically; industry moved from net importer to net exporter
items.quote: The demand fundamentally is robust for us in India, a large percentage of the demand is domestic itself. As an industry, we have moved from being net importers to net exporters.

items.statement: PVC demand muted globally and in India; prices under downward pressure from abundant imports
items.quote: Global as well as Indian PVC demand was muted in the key geographies & prices remained soft in the period. PVC pricing continued to witness downward pressure given abundant imports and global oversupply.

items.statement: Hydrogen peroxide demand stable from pulp, paper, textiles, water treatment but domestic market oversupplied
items.quote: Hydrogen peroxide demand was broadly stable, underpinned by strong offtake from pulp and paper, textiles, and water treatment. However, the domestic market remained oversupplied with new facilities being commissioned and dumping from Bangladesh.

items.statement: Epichlorohydrin demand firm supported by structurally strong consumption and epoxy resin capacity increases
items.quote: Epichlorohydrin demand stood firm, supported by structurally strong consumption as well as increase in capacity of epoxy resins.

items.statement: Chemicals PBDIT down 8% YoY due to higher fixed costs and new plant stabilization, partly offset by lower input prices
items.quote: PBDIT was down by 8% due to higher fixed costs given business growth & stabilization costs of new plants, partly offset by lower input prices and better operating

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT lower at Rs 19 cr vs Rs 29 cr YoY due to lower PVC and carbide prices despite better operating costs
items.quote: PBDIT was lower at Rs 19 crores as compared to Rs 29 crores last year, due to lower prices despite better operating costs due to power & carbon material.

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT down to Rs 35 cr from Rs 43 cr YoY due to product mix, higher fixed costs from new investments, and aluminum price lag
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was down at Rs 35 cr as against Rs 43 cr last year. This was due to product mix and higher fixed costs owing to investments in growing newer revenue platforms, enhancing brand presence and acquisition related costs, partially offset by increase in volumes.

items.statement: Shriram Farm Solutions PBDIT down 11% YoY due to moderation in research wheat margins from poor kharif season
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was down by 11% mainly due to moderation in research wheat margins owing to poor kharif season leading to lower product prices.

items.statement: Fertilizer PBDIT down to Rs 20 cr from Rs 29 cr YoY on lower gas prices ($13.2 vs $14.5/mmbtu)
items.quote: Gas prices were down at $13.2/mmbtu in Q3 FY26 vs $14.5/mmbtu last year. Consequently, PBDIT was also down at Rs 20 crores vs Rs 29 crores last year.

items.statement: Bioseed PBDIT up 73% YoY on better corn and paddy volumes, higher prices, and Rs 10 cr gain from vegetable R&D germplasm sale
items.quote: Accordingly, PBDIT for the quarter was up by 73% year on year.

items.statement: Vinyl margins helped by reduction in power costs (60-70% of production cost) over last 1-1.5 years
items.quote: See, one, our power costs have come down. So as you know, power is the almost 60%, 70% cost of production. So we have seen reduction in our power cost and that is continuous, if you see last 1, 1.5 years, our power costs have been coming down.

items.statement: Chlorine prices under pressure; caustic soda and chlorine downstream customers impacted by geopolitical factors and tariffs
items.quote: However, chlorine prices have been under pressure. Caustic soda and chlorine downstream customers have been impacted by geopolitical factors, including tariffs.

items.statement: Government levied anti-dumping duties on Liquid Epoxy Resin in November 2025; actively pursuing MIP for PVC and QCO for potable applications
items.quote: The Government of India also levied Anti -dumping duties on Liquid Epoxy Resin in November '25 which should start having impact in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Industry urging government for higher sugar MSP, higher ethanol blending targets, and sufficient sugarcane feedstock allocation
items.quote: Industry is urging government for support through increase in sugar MSP & higher blending targets of ethanol as well as sufficient allocation of sugarcane feedstock to ensure mills viability amid increasing costs of production.

items.statement: Outstanding fertilizer subsidy Rs 116 cr as of 31 Dec 2025 vs Rs 111 cr a year ago
items.quote: Outstanding fertilizer subsidy was Rs 116 crores on 31st December 2025 as against Rs 111 crores last year.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 1,084 cr as of 31 Dec 2025 vs Rs 867 cr a year ago; down from Rs 1,395 cr as of 31 Mar 2025 on sugar inventory reduction
items.quote: The company’s net debt is at Rs 1,084 crores as on 31st December, 2025 as against Rs 867 crores as on 31st December, 2024 and Rs 1,395 crore s as on 31st March

items.statement: Interim dividend of 180% (Rs 56.14 cr) declared; total dividend for year 360% (Rs 112.28 cr)
items.quote: Board announced an interim dividend of 180% amounting to Rs. 56.14 crores. This took the total dividend announced for the year to 360% amounting to Rs 112.28 crores.

items.statement: Sugar recovery better by 0.4-0.5% vs last year; further improvement expected if trend continues
items.quote: Yes. So compared to last year, we are better by about 0.4%, 0.5%. Now if the trend continues, yes, we should be better in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Ethanol offers for 2025-26 season at 1,777 crore litres (1.7x OMC requirement); 72% grain-based, 28% sugarcane-based
items.quote: OMCs received 1,777 crore litre of ethanol offers for the 2025 -26 season, which is 1.70 times of the total requirement tendered by OMCs. Allocation is led by grain -based feedstocks i.e. 72% and balance 28% from sugarcane.

items.statement: Sugar margins expected lower at current prices due to higher SAP costs; pursuing policy support for MSP, exports, ethanol allocation
items.quote: But as of now, yes, margins will be lower than what they have been till now at current prices.

items.statement: Semiconductor business targets consistent revenue growth over next 4 quarters, ASIC pipeline over $100M by Q4, EBIT neutral in FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, our marke rs remain unchanged from the last quarter, which is consistent revenue growth over the next 4 quarters, integrating Kinetic Technologies, an ASIC pipeline of over $100 million by Q4 and becoming EBIT neutral in FY27

items.statement: DET targets 15% EBIT margin by Q4 FY27 with current business mix
items.quote: On the EBIT part, we had talked about Q4 of FY 2027 with our current business mix that we have is what our target is.

items.statement: Semiconductor Q4 loss expected to continue at $2-3M range, organic breakeven targeted for FY27
items.quote: That is correct. We will not see any upside from the deals that we won or from the inorganic. So, yes, there will be a loss in Q4 along those lines. Like I said, our goal is to break even in FY27, and we are on track for that.

items.statement: DET EBIT margin expanded 25 bps QoQ to 12.4% in Q3 despite wage hikes
items.quote: On EBIT front, the normalized DET EBIT for Q3 came in at 12.4%, which is a 25-bps expansion quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: DLM delivered double-digit EBITDA margins, up 207 bps YoY in Q3
items.quote: But I will say that over the years, we have talked about the criticality of that business delivering double -digit EBITDA margins , a nd this quarter, we delivered double-digit EBITDA margins. They grew 207 basis points year -over-year

items.statement: DET grew 1.9% QoQ and flattish YoY in constant currency; USD growth 1.5% QoQ and 0.9% YoY
items.quote: Cyient DET grew 1.9% quarter-over-quarter and flattish year-over-year, about 0.7% down in constant currency terms, which is 1.5% quarter-over-quarter and 0.9% year-over-year growth in USD terms.

items.statement: Transportation grew 2.9% QoQ, Network & Infrastructure grew 2.5% QoQ, Strategic Units flattish with -0.2% QoQ
items.quote: Transportation and grew by 2.9% quarter-over-quarter; and Network and Infrastructure grew 2.5% quarter-over-quarter driven by focused account mining and sales approaches across value chain of our customers. Strategic Units cluster remained flattish Q3 with a marginal drop of 0.2% in line with our anticipation.

items.statement: Semiconductor order intake up 36% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Order intake is up 36% year-on-year, which is a healthy indicator for the business.

items.statement: DLM book-to-bill ratio >1 for 3 consecutive quarters, strong order book momentum
items.quote: Our order book momentum remains strong. We had a book-to-bill ratio of more than 1 for 3 consecutive quarters, which means that we have a very strong order book.

items.statement: DET large deals funnel highest ever in company history, key accounts grew 5% QoQ and 15.5% YoY
items.quote: We have a robust funnel buildup over the last few months, with large deals funnel being the highest ever in Cyient history. Our key accounts continue to demonstrate strong revenue growth with a 5% quarter-over-quarter and 15.5% year-over-year growth performance.

items.statement: Diversifying from mechanical engineering into software, platform software, data engineering, AI; tech pipeline in significant double digits as % of total
items.quote: So, I think we have a robust pipeline which is built up for technology, as we call it, which is in significant double digits as a percentage of our pipeline. So, we think that both from the wins that we have talked about, the funnel that we have for near-term closure, we are definitely seeing a diversification in our services portfolio

items.statement: Acquiring majority stake in Kinetic Technologies (250 products, 100+ patents) for analog/power semiconductor leadership
items.quote: Some key achievements include the strengthening of our analog and power leadership through a definitive agreement to acquire a majority in Kinetic Technologies, who are a leader in high-performance analog, mixed signal and analog semiconductors for power-related applications. They have 250 products and over 100 patents.

items.statement: Selected as preferred partner for SCL fab modernization under MeitY's INR 4,500 crore semiconductor program
items.quote: We also secured a strategic role in the modernization of India's oldest integrated semiconductor fab, SCL. This is under MeitY's semiconductor program. Cyient semiconductors has been selected as the preferred partner for the critical package centered around technology, IP, design enablement and automation responsibilities.

items.statement: Hired Harjott Atrii as Chief Business Officer and Bhabesh Acharya as Chief AI Architect to accelerate technology growth
items.quote: this quarter, we also worked on adding to our leadership strength with 2 key hires focused on the growth trajectory for technology. Harjott Atrii joined us as a Chief Business Officer, responsible for technology growth and high -growth markets, which we could not cover in the past. Bhabesh Acharya joined us as the Chief AI architect , responsible for building depth and differentiation in our Data

items.statement: DET FCF to normalized PAT conversion at 158% in Q3, net cash position INR 1,434 crores (highest in 9 quarters)
items.quote: Our cash conversion per DET continues to remain very strong. Our net cash position for DET at the end of Q3 stood at INR 1,434 crores, which is the highest net cash position we have had over the last 9 quarters.

items.statement: One-time INR 40 crore provision for new labor codes compliance (gratuity liabilities) taken as exceptional item in Q3
items.quote: We have taken a one-time provision of INR 40 crores in Q3 towards truing up our past period provision for liabilities such as gratuity, resulting from this regulatory change.

items.statement: Macro events and account-specific risks (e.g., top customer CEO change halted initiatives) remain key risks to deal closures
items.quote: For example, in Q3, we were impacted by one of our top customers' CEO change, which happened, which put a halt to several of the initiatives that we were expecting to close in the last quarter. items.statement: Semiconductor revenue grew 10.7% QoQ on top of 12% previous quarter, margins stabilized though still loss-making
items.quote: We delivered strong Q3 growth, 10.7% on top of 12% in the previous quarter. Order intake is up 36% year-on-year, which is a healthy indicator for the business. And though we are still loss-making, margins have stabilized over the last quarter.

items.statement: Fully mitigated third tranche of wage hikes impact through cost optimization and revenue momentum
items.quote: The headwinds we had in this quarter include the third tranche of wage hikes for the year, and we are happy to report that we were able to fully mitigate this impact with the ongoing cost optimization program and the recovering revenue momentum, which is very clearly visible.

items.statement: Semiconductor partnership with Navitas for GaN chips targeting AI data centers, launched indigenous ARKA GKT-1 chip for smart utilities
items.quote: With the partnership with Navitas, we will now be able to bring high-voltage, high-power GaN chips to India, which again, like I said, are critical for AI data centers and AI infrastructure. We also launched India's first indigenous silicon platform for smart utilities. This was developed with Azimuth AI, a chip called ARKA GKT-1.

items.statement: Recognized as ISG leader in manufacturing services globally and in power/utilities for smart metering and grid modernization in North America
items.quote: Cyient was recognized in 2 major categories by ISG, firstly as a leader in manufacturing services and solutions globally; and second, in power and utilities for smart metering and grid modernization for North America.

items.statement: DET H2 margins will be better than H1 margins; not commenting on full year exit margin
items.quote: But I will just repeat what we said in the previous call, our H2 margins will be better than H1 margins.

items.statement: Aerospace growth driven by MRO/aftermarket services, commercial aviation volume ramp-up, new midsized aircraft designs, and digital programs across manufacturing/supply chain
items.quote: Of course, with no major designs which are going on at this point in time, a large part of it is driven by MRO and aftermarket services. Many of our customers are experiencing significant volume ramp-up that they have to deliver with the growth in commercial aviation, and that is driving a large part of the growth.

items.statement: Pipeline evenly distributed across US, Europe, APAC; large deals across North America and Western Europe
items.quote: From a pipeline view perspective, it is quite evenly distributed, which is reflective of the current distribution of our revenue across the U.S., Europe, and Asia-Pacific. And from a large deal perspective, it is both across North America and Western Europe.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty could delay deal processes if extended for weeks/months; customers have more robust mechanisms now
items.quote: But if it gets extended and drags out for a few weeks or months, obviously, it delays some of the deal processes. But if it is just a one-week surge and quietening down, that should not make a huge impact on our deal cycles, so to speak.

items.statement: DET normalized PAT INR 150 crores, up 9% QoQ and 40% YoY
items.quote: The DET normalized PAT for the quarter is at INR 150 crores, representing a healthy 9% growth quarter-on-quarter, and a 40% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect enterprise and data center revenue share to move from 20% to 30% in next 12-18 months
items.quote: we do expect this ratio that we spoke about 20% to move towards 30% in probably next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Directional target of 20% EBITDA margin for Optical Networking business at 70%+ utilization
items.quote: Directionally, this is a business where if we operate with the right utilizations of 70% plus, we are confident that ultimately, this is a business that should be 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.3% due to 760 bps tariff impact; underlying margin 17.9%
items.quote: Operational EBITDA has improved for 5 consecutive quarters, rising from 11.2% in Q2 of FY '25 to 17.9% in Q3 of FY '26, driven by a richer product mix and a higher contribution from the U.S. market. items.statement: YTD FY26 EBITDA grew 35% YoY to INR 410 crores with margin 12.4%
items.quote: For YTD FY '26, EBITDA grew 35% YoY to INR410 crores, with margins improving to 12.4% YoY.

items.statement: Open order book INR 5,325 crores, up from INR 5,188 crores in Q2; INR 988 crores for next quarter execution
items.quote: Our open order book stood at INR5,325 crores, up from INR5,188 crores in Q2 FY '26, reflecting healthy order inflows and strong market confidence. Of this, INR 988 crores is slated for execution in the next quarter, while the remaining INR 4,337 crores is scheduled for execution over FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: YTD FY26 order intake INR 4,263 crores, up 40.3% YoY
items.quote: YTD FY '26, we have recorded INR4,263 crores in orders, a strong 40.3% growth over last year.

items.statement: North America revenue share increased from 25% to 36%; Europe at 40%
items.quote: North America share increased from 25% in FY '25 to 36% in the current financial year, while Europe remains a significant contributor at 40%.

items.statement: CRU projects North America 13.7% CAGR through 2030; APAC ex-China ~6% CAGR
items.quote: CRU expects it to deliver the strongest regional growth of 13.7% CAGR through 2030. APAC, excluding China, is the second major growth pillar, growing at almost 6% CAGR led by India and Southeast Asia.

items.statement: Invested over $50 million in U.S. manufacturing facility
items.quote: Look, I think if you have seen the investments we have done, I think, more than $50 million of investment to build a factory of a certain scale.

items.statement: U.S. facility currently serves only part of North America revenue; not sufficient for full demand
items.quote: So currently, it is only a part of revenue. So, it is a lengthy process to qualify your manufacturing unit for all the standard products which we do

items.statement: Utilizations improved QoQ; glass operations mindful of germanium availability
items.quote: But broadly, what we can share is that the utilizations have improved QoQ. One thing that we are mindful of, particularly in our glass operations, is availability of germanium.

items.statement: Tariff impact 760 bps on Q3 EBITDA; mitigation includes passing cost to customers and ramping U.S. production
items.quote: However, the U.S. tariff reset effective mid Q2 of FY '26 created a temporary headwind, reducing reported EBITDA by almost 760 bps in Q3 of the current fiscal and bringing the reported margins to 10.3%. While underlying margin momentum remains strong, we have proactively started implementing some mitigation measures, such as passing on some proportion of tariff cost to customers and aggressively r

items.statement: OFC and cable prices stable globally; no decline; focused on long-term contracts not spot market
items.quote: From the pricing perspective, I think, overall, it has been stable. It has been steady, both in China as well as in globally. So, I don't see any concern on that side. And as we said, that ultimately for players like us who are supplying into Europe and U.S., we are focused on long-term contracts with our customers.

items.statement: Enterprise and data center revenue 20% of YTD FY26; target 30% in 12-18 months
items.quote: Our enterprise and data center business is gaining traction with 20% revenue contribution in YTD FY '26, and we remain on track to scale this to 30% and expect it to be a key growth driver in the medium term.

items.statement: Optical connectivity attach rate moderated to 17% YTD FY26 from 22% FY25 due to mix and timing
items.quote: Our optical connectivity attaches rates moderated to 17% in year-to-date FY '26 from 22% in FY '25. This was primarily driven by product mix and project timing, along with a sharp acceleration in OFC revenues leading to a higher base.

items.statement: STL Digital added major customer, total base 34; won USD multimillion SAP S/4HANA deal with US healthcare major
items.quote: During Q3, we added a new major customer, taking our total base to 34 and secured U.S. dollar multimillion SAP S/4HANA deal with U.S. -based health care major, demonstrating execution capability in large complex programs.

items.statement: Global ex-China OFC market share stable at 8% YTD FY26
items.quote: Our global ex- China OFC market share remains stable at 8% YTD FY '26, reflecting disciplined execution in a competitive market with clear focus on gaining our share over time through our technologies.

items.statement: Net debt INR 1,331 crores; debt-to-equity 0.87; net debt/EBITDA 2.58x
items.quote: Net debt stands at INR1,331 crores with debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87 and net debt to EBITDA at 2.58x.

items.statement: STL Digital team 1,120 consultants
items.quote: Our team now comprise of 1,120 consultants supporting growth deal sizes and multiservice engagements.

items.statement: STL Digital open order book INR 276 crores

items.statement: SMS volumes growing; winning net new customers; OTT business growing and recognised as Meta partner of the year
items.quote: If you look at the volumes on the SMS side, our volumes are growing. We have, in fact winning a lot of new customers, and we have added net new customers to our portfolio, and those customers have ramped up.

items.statement: Focused on more profitable routes and customers sending messages outside India, bringing additional profitability
items.quote: We focused on more profitable routes. We focused on customers sending messages to outside of India, and we've grown that. That has also brought in some additional profitability.

items.statement: OTT business growing; recognised as Meta partner of the year; charging for additional services like bots
items.quote: On the OTT side, you must be aware, as we speak today, we have been recognised by Meta as the partner of the year. So, we are their most preferred partners now.

items.quote: When they see there's a strong demand, they would increase the prices, okay? So, there's nothing new that is happening on the ad business also, and that is happening here as well.

items.quote: See, for a customer to fully ramp up, it takes good three, four quarters once we onboard a customer. I also mentioned a couple of quarters back that we are focusing on our existing customers also to increase our wallet share, where we are already present.

items.statement: Innovation engine working on platform to go live by end of quarter; will update shareholders when live with telcos and enterprises
items.quote: Our innovation team is working on a platform which have to go live by end of this quarter. And as and when we go live with both telcos and enterprises, we should be able to update our shareholders.

items.statement: CPaaS market growing at 8-12% YoY; digital adoption and UPI transactions driving growth; geographical expansion aspirations to increase TAM

items.quote: If you really look at the international players, they don't have much presence left in India anymore, which we predicted three years back as well.

items.quote: And likewise, if you look at OTT, now the focus is not only on the top 200 or 300 large enterprise customers, who are into B2C business, but TAM is increasing to SMEs.

items.quote: we are trying to focus on accounts based on the wallet share that we have and not just on the large customer cohort, but also customers which are between 20 million to 50 million per month kind of number that we generate from them

items.statement: Near-term pricing stability assumed but competitive environment remains active with continuous pricing pressure; long-term view difficult
items.quote: in the near future, we would want to assume that t here will be stability. However, having said that, competition environment is stil l active, and there is a continuous pricing

items.statement: ValueFirst International acquisition awaiting regulatory approvals; responding to regulator questions; no timeline given

items.quote: Firstly, I would say that, you asked for what would be the impact on our top line and bottom line. So I would say the impact is not material, it's not much, if we really lose it.

items.quote: Already we worked for more than three months to activate our bots for more than 55 various government departments in Tamil Nadu. They are very, very happy with it. And the service has been launched.

items.statement: Many more states in pipeline for similar e-governance projects; ValueFirst primary provider for WhatsApp services at NIC and growing well
items.quote: Yeah. We have many more states in the pipeline and working with other states as well.

items.statement: No guidance given on top line or margins; aspiring to continue building on growth momentum
items.quote: We would not want to give any guidance or any number, sorry, because it will be forward-looking. But as we said, we are aspiring to continue to build on our growth momentum, and I think it should continue.

items.statement: Focus equally on enterprise and platform segments; growing continuously on both
items.quote: On both. Rahil, we are focusing on both segments, and we would see that on both of them, we are growing continuously. So, focus is there on both the segments.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with good cash balance; investing in existing TAM growth and new innovations internally; not incubating unrelated businesses
items.quote: We have a strong balance sheet. We have good cash balance. And honestly, our efforts are more to do with addressing the existing TAM currently because it is growing at a decent pace.

items.statement: Increasing investor engagement with domestic mutual funds and foreign institutional investors now that growth momentum demonstrated
items.quote: And now that the growth momentum is back, we obviously have taken a note of this internally. Also, we have discussed that as management, we would want to go out and engage with both the domestic funds as well as foreign institutional investors.

items.statement: RERA funds unlocking from FY27, cash utilization to begin then

items.statement: DCCDL dividend payout ratio to remain at 75-80% of PAT for FY26-27
items.quote: the dividend payout, whatever percentage of the PAT was there last year, we at least propose to the Board to continue at that level for FY '26 and FY '27. Abhinav Sinha: In DCCDL? Sriram Khattar: That is in the ballpark of 75%-80

items.statement: FY26 sales volume guidance of 4 lakh tons achievable with Q4 volume of 1.3 lakh tons
items.quote: we are very sure that we will cross 2.5 lakh tons of sales and the before mentioned target of 4 lakh tons will be achieved in this financial year itself.

items.statement: FY27 sales volume guidance of 6.5 lakh tons, FY28 of 9 lakh tons
items.quote: the next year target of 6.5 lakh tons will be achieved and the target after that of around 9 lakh tons sales, that will be achieved as well. We are sticking to our targets.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs.4,500-5,000
items.quote: we will aim to get EBITDA per ton of Rs.4,500-5,000 EBITDA per ton for the full year.

items.statement: FY27 DFT segment EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs.6,500
items.quote: when we are impaneled everywhere, we are expecting that we will achieve a EBITDA per ton of Rs.6,500 in DFT segment itself.

items.statement: FY27 exports target of 60,000-65,000 metric tons
items.quote: Exports, we will be targeting around 60,000 to 65,000 tons of sales for next year.

items.statement: RCI Industries FY26 Q4 sales target of 500 metric tons (Rs.50-60 crores revenue)
items.quote: the target for this quarter is that we will do close to 500 MT of sales in RCI, and that will equate to around Rs.50 to 60 crores of top line in that segment.

items.statement: RCI Industries FY27 sales target of 500 metric tons/month (H2 FY27)
items.quote: going ahead, our target is that we will reach 500 MT of sales per month. And that should be happening starting H2 of next financial year.

items.statement: RCI Industries FY27 EBITDA margin target of 10%
items.quote: we are very confident that we will achieve 10% EBITDA margins starting H2 of next financial year.

items.statement: RCI Industries FY27 revenue contribution of Rs.4,500-5,000 crores
items.quote: we should be touching close to 4,500-5,000 tons of sales of material in RCI for the next financial year.

items.statement: FY26 capex of Rs.250 crores (Rs.130-140 crores spent in 9M FY26)
items.quote: For the FY26, the total CAPEX spend is close to Rs.250 crores. Out of that, Rs.130-140 crores have already been spent.

items.statement: FY27 capex of Rs.100 crores (excluding API capex)
items.quote: going ahead, next year, Rs.100 crores of CAPEX will be spent as we already planned, and plus the CAPEX of API as well.

items.statement: API capex of Rs.75 crores
items.quote: for API, we will be doing a CAPEX of close to Rs.75 crores.

items.statement: Wider segment capex of Rs.150-170 crores pending
items.quote: close to Rs.150-170 crores of CAPEX is still pending on that side.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 sales volume expected to cross 2.5 lakh tons due to restocking demand and government tenders
items.quote: Already, we have achieved a sales volume of 40,000 tons in this quarter. So, given the run rate of this quarter, we are very sure that we will cross 2.5 lakh tons of sales.

items.statement: Government tenders expected to boost demand in FY27
items.quote: as the new budget is expected, there will be new tenders coming to the market as well in which we will participate, and accordingly, there will be more orders.

items.statement: HRC price increase expected to drive restocking demand in Q4 FY26
items.quote: there is restocking demand happening as well. And more than the restocking happening in the dealer segment, there is also much more demand coming from the government side as well.

items.statement: HRC price increase expected in February FY26 (Rs.2/ton)
items.quote: we are expecting a price hike happening in the month of February as well; around Rs.2 price hike is expected in the next month.

items.statement: Price gap between primary and secondary steel to widen with HRC price increases
items.quote: as we see the more price increase happening in HRC, the price gap will increase as well from primary to secondary.

items.statement: DFT segment EBITDA per ton of Rs.4,500-5,000 in Q3 FY26, Rs.5,500-6,500 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: in this quarter, we should be having EBITDA per ton of Rs.5,500 to Rs.6,500 in DFT segment.

items.statement: FY27 value-added product mix of 35-40%
items.quote: it will be around 35-40% value added and the remaining will be generally.

items.statement: Government payment delays for Jal Jeevan Mission orders (2.5-3 months typical)
items.quote: on worst case scenario, the payment comes in 2.5-3 months. There might be small parts of payment in small proportions, which are held back for more than six-seven months.

items.statement: INR 500 crore annualized revenue in ongoing quarter
items.quote: I am encouraged to report that we have achieved an annualized revenue run rate of INR 460 crores and on track to reach INR 500 crores in the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: 8-10% profitability at INR 1,000 crore revenue in 3 years
items.quote: At INR 1,000 crores, we will be looking at 8% to 10% profitability at the least. That is how we are currently gearing up.

items.statement: PropTiger contributed INR 30 crore revenue in Q3 FY26
items.quote: PropTiger contributed approximately INR 30 crores of revenue in this quarter.

items.statement: 11 active mandates in PropTiger, 20% of revenue
items.quote: specifically called out the mandates because this is the highest-ever mandates that PropTiger has had over the last two to three years and we are growing that business. There is good profitability in that business segment. However, still, mandate would account for around 20% of the revenue

items.statement: 30% EBITDA margin improvement in NestAway after pruning exercise
items.quote: We have 30% improvement in terms of our EBITDA margin in the specific business for the December month specifically, where this entire rationalization exercise has been now completed.

items.statement: Distribution segment profitable for past few quarters, rental segment improving
items.quote: the distribution segment has been in black for a considerable amount of time now for the past few quarters, and it will continue to be so. Taking a leaf from that, we are also now ensuring and focusing on taking the rental business towards profitability

items.statement: Rental demand driven by IT hubs and student accommodation near colleges
items.quote: We are focused on young professionals and students. So, there are specific key micro-markets in the region, which are near to IT hubs, and student accommodation, which is near colleges and educational hubs, which is where we typically target to acquire assets.

items.statement: Rental growth headwinds in Kota, shifting focus to family rentals and co-living
items.quote: There were some headwinds that the rental business faced, especially in the student living business. And the growth that we had expected from some cities like Kota did not come through.

items.statement: Win PIN Code strategy for hyper-local market domination in rental segment
items.quote: We have adopted something called as Win a PIN Code strategy from a go-to-market standpoint, where the focus is going hyper-local in terms of market domination.

items.statement: Interest cost of INR 8 crore/quarter, INR 2 crore actual loan interest, rest IndAS impact
items.quote: The interest cost that we see in the financial statement, has two parts. Out of the INR 8 crores, INR 2 crores is the actual interest cost that we pay on the loans, specifically lease rental discounting against the buildings we have.

items.statement: No inbound investment opportunities for sum-of-the-parts businesses
items.quote: we haven't gone to market to raise capital or seek investors. I mean, there hasn't been any inbound opportunity that has come for investment in any of the sum of the parts or the subsidiary

items.statement: SM REIT license acquired in July 2025, evaluating assets for launch
items.quote: We have acquired the license in July 2025 for the SM REIT registration. We are currently building a strong pipeline of assets, which we believe will be the right fit for the SM REIT as an investment product.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated capacity utilization to average 63-64%, Q4 FY26 > Q3 FY26
items.quote: For the current year, I think we'll close average utilization levels of 63%, 64% for the entire year. Q4 utilization should be hopefully upwards of Q3 utilization levels.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated capacity utilization to reach 70%+
items.quote: And for FY27, we intend to reach capital utilization of almost 70% plus.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to reach 15-20% in upcoming quarters
items.quote: On a long-term basis, I've always said that EBITDA margin of anywhere around 15% to 20% is easily sustainable in the industry. And hopefully, we intend to reach those margins in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: MP plant capex to start in next quarter, operational in 10-12 months
items.quote: So the MP plant capex, we intend to start hopefully in the running quarter. And the plant operationalization will take a period of almost 10 to 12 months.

items.statement: MP plant capex estimated at Rs. 75-80 crore, execution over next 12 months
items.quote: So we are planning to put up a plant in Madhya Pradesh with an installed capacity of around 2,00,000 to 2,50,000 cubic meters per annum. And the total capex for this facility will be in the tune of almost Rs. 75 crores to Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: Bulk orders from select customers (e.g., L&T) for 6-9 month delivery
items.quote: We keep on getting bulk orders from select few customers, the likes L&T or a few big corporates who place bulk orders which is for a delivery schedule of 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 11.1% in Q3 FY26 (vs. 2.8% Q2 FY26, 10.8% Q3 FY25)
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY26 was Rs. 81 million, up 31.8% year-on-year with margins expanding to 11.1% compared to 2.8% and 10.8% in Q2 FY26 and Q3 FY25, respectively.

items.statement: Average realizations up 2-3% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The average realization has just gone up by around 2% to 3% for this quarter.

items.statement: Construction activity improving; demand expected to remain supportive in upcoming quarters
items.quote: At the industry level, construction activity is expected to remain supporting in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: AAC wall panel utilization at 10% (of 51% total plant utilization), targeting 30-40% in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: And we should be able to keep on improving the capacity utilization in that plant and improving the sales of AAC wall panels over the next 3 to 4 quarters to reach 30%, 40% plus.

items.statement: Construction chemicals contributed 5-7% of revenue in Q3 FY26
items.quote: From the construction chemicals, around 5% to 7% of the revenue was contributed by the construction chemicals.

items.statement: FY27 earnings growth to improve from Q1 FY27 due to lower slippages and higher paying book
items.quote: starting Q1 of next year with the entire remaining bad book going out, we will naturally see an uptick in our earnings.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 earnings growth to be higher than Q3 FY26 due to improving paying book
items.quote: Q4 will certainly be much better than Q3, even where we stand today. And that is largely because of the fact that there has been a steady increase in my paying book.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 slippages expected to be ~Rs. 100 crores (Bank level)
items.quote: we expect that our slippages will be about Rs. 100 crores and thereabouts for Q4.

items.statement: MFI slippages in Q4 FY26 expected to be ~Rs. 75-80 crores, retail asset slippages ~Rs. 20-25 crores
items.quote: for IF as a whole, it will be around 75 to 80 and around Rs. 20-odd crores or less, little less for the retail asset business.

items.statement: MFI monthly slippages to reduce to ~Rs. 20 crores by March FY26
items.quote: the target is to have less than Rs. 20 crores, which is used to be what, well, before the entire mini crisis started

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to improve below 65% in FY27
items.quote: in the next financial year, we are able to come well below the 65% mark.

items.statement: Credit cost to stabilize at ~1% in steady state
items.quote: with the kind of mix that we have today in our portfolio in the Bank, we would want to have a credit cost of not more than 1%.

items.statement: CGFMU claims of ~Rs. 200-300 crores expected in Q1 FY27
items.quote: the largest chunk would be claimed in the Q1, which may be around closer to Rs. 200 crores to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: NIMs to stabilize at ~7.5%-8% in next quarters
items.quote: we expect the NIMs to be around 7.5% to 8%.

items.statement: ROE to reach ~10% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: run rate will be closer to around 11% in Q4, 10% above and probably closer to 11%.

items.statement: ROA to reach ~1.1% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: ROA of around 10 is the first thing that we would like to achieve before we really project for the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Inclusive finance disbursements at ~Rs. 500 crores/month
items.quote: disbursements have largely returned to earlier run rates with the business now clocking closer to Rs. 500 crores per month.

items.statement: Vikas loan disbursements in 9M FY26 at Rs. 2,729 crores
items.quote: Vikas loan disbursements during 9M FY26 stood at Rs. 2,729 crores, reflecting sustained Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle portfolio grew 35% YoY to Rs. 1,609 crores by Dec’25
items.quote: The commercial vehicle portfolio grew from Rs. 1,190 crores in December 2024 to Rs. 1,609 crores in Dec’25, registering a year-on growth of 35%.

items.statement: Mortgage book grew 39% YoY to Rs. 2,778 crores by Dec’25
items.quote: The mortgage book, which includes micro-mortgages, expanded from Rs. 1,999 crores in December 2024 to Rs. 2,778 crores as of Dec’25, growing by 39% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Unsecured business loan portfolio run rate at Rs. 20 crores/month
items.quote: unsecured business loan portfolio is growing at a healthy and calibrated pace, which is now clocking a run rate of Rs. 20 crores per month.

items.statement: Credit on UPI customer onboarding at 2.2 lakh active customers in one quarter
items.quote: customer onboarding growing exponentially with 2.2 lakh active customers in one quarter.

items.statement: Nominal GDP growth projection for FY27

items.statement: FY26 gross margin trajectory of 50%+

items.statement: Q4 FY26 margins healthier than prior quarters
items.quote: our margin expectations on the deliveries we will make in the quarter will be healthier than all our previous quarters this year.

items.statement: Defense procurement tailwind from INR20,000 crore ISR/loitering munition/strike drone outlay
items.quote: recent reports of a fresh procurement outlay of around INR20,000 crores across ISR platforms, loitering munitions and strike drones provide a strong multiyear demand tailwind for the domestic drone industry.

items.statement: No large FY26 Q4 order inflows beyond YTD INR440 crore

items.statement: Supply chain constraints due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: we are observing certain supply side constraints, and we are working closely with our supply chain partners to navigate the dynamic challenges.

items.statement: Lumpy revenue profile due to large defense contracts

items.statement: ZOLT/YETI prototypes flying in H1/H2 FY26
items.quote: the propulsion testing version of the YETI platform is going to fly within the first half of this year and an advanced prototype, again, we expect to fly towards the end of the year

items.statement: No forward guidance provided for next quarter or FY27
items.quote: We don't know what will happen the next quarter and I think I will say that since the time we have started doing our roadshows for the IPO, we actually don't give any guidance because we don't know whether there will be an earthquake or there will be a flood or suddenly in December, we saw a large amount of claims, especially due to fog, which happened suddenly.

items.statement: GDPI growth of 20.9% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: GDPI is about Rs. 2,557 crores compared to Rs. 2,115 crores, which is a growth of 20.9.

items.statement: Two-wheeler business grew 47% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: New business in two-wheeler only in this Quarter 3 and you will remember that lower GST was introduced from 22nd September. Digit is a fairly large player on two-wheeler business. So our two wheeler business only in Q3 grew by 47%, where collected premium in this quarter was Rs. 668 crore against Rs. 456 crores of last year.

items.statement: Motor business mix increased to 66% in Q3 FY26 (vs. 60% YoY)
items.quote: In terms of overall business mix, I think this has been quite a quarter for Digit, where in Q3, the motor business has touched 66% compared to 60% of last year.

items.statement: Motor product mix: Private car 47%, two-wheeler 34%, CV 19% (all-time low)
items.quote: Within motor in this quarter, now CV is in all-time low for Digit. So out of 100% of the motor business, private car now is 47%, two-wheeler is 34%, which will be probably the highest motor component amongst all the large companies. And CV is at all-time low of 19%.

items.statement: Health, travel, and PA business de-grew 31% YoY in Q3 FY26 due to exiting government health business
items.quote: In motor, OD, TP, fire, others, our growth rate is a significantly better than the industry. But in case of Health, Travel and PA, the industry grew by 28.7% while we de-grew by about 31% essentially because of this reason.

items.statement: IFRS combined ratio improved to 105 in Q3 FY26 (vs. 106.2 YoY)
items.quote: If you look at the combined ratio, in Quarter 3 under IFRS basis, the combined ratio is 105, which last year in the same quarter was 106.2.

items.statement: Profit before tax increased 37% to Rs. 163 crore in Q3 FY26 (Rs. 170 crore without one-time wage code impact)
items.quote: The profit before tax has jumped to 37% to Rs. 163 crores compared to Rs. 119 crores during the previous quarter. Now, the impact of new wage code in this quarter is about one time Rs. 7 crores. So this also is impacting the IGAAP COR by 0.3%. If this was not there, the profit would have actually increased to Rs. 170 crores compared to Rs. 119 crores

items.statement: IFRS profit estimated at Rs. 781 crore for 9M FY26 (IGAAP profit Rs. 459 crore + DAC Rs. 322 crore)
items.quote: Profit, say for 9 months, Rs. 459 crores, which is IGAAP add Rs. 322 crores deferred acquisition cost (DAC), you hit a figure of Rs. 781 crores.

items.statement: Electric two-wheeler claims risk higher due to total loss in floods; reinsurance cost is an expense, not income
items.quote: So Sanketh, this is more an expense item rather than an income item because as I said we have taken this this year. As of now, there is no claims recovery in the treaty yet. So we have paid a cost for the option. The auction is not in the money yet. It's reducing the profit rather than increasing the profit

items.statement: AUM crossed Rs. 22,509 crore in Q3 FY26 (up 18.8% YoY)
items.quote: AUM as I said, have already increased to Rs. 22,500 crores. And compared to December 31 st, 2024, this is an increase of roughly $35.7 billion, savings in Rs. 2800 crores, which is a growth of about 18.8%.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 230% (vs. required 150%)
items.quote: Solvency is about 230% against required of 150%, which is good.

items.statement: Bus contribution margin may dip 1-2 percentage points from current 45% but not below 30%
items.quote: I think we'll be comfortable operating even a couple of percentage points, 1 or 2 percentage points lower than this even there. But we would not want this to go into the 30s, just to give you some comfort on that.

items.statement: International flights GTV grew over 50% YoY, now 20% of total flights GTV; strong Tier 2/3 demand for Southeast Asia/Middle East routes
items.quote: International flights GTV grew over 50% Y-o-Y in Q3 and has now crossed 20% of our overall flights GTV for the quarter. This growth is no longer restricted to Tier 1 airports. We are seeing strong demand from Tier 2 and 3 cities, driven by improving connectivity to Southeast Asia and the Middle East, both through direct routes and efficient one-stop connections.

items.statement: Spiritual tourism (Varanasi, Tirupati, Prayagraj, Ayodhya, Shirdi) growing with Gen Z participation via bus/train
items.quote: Destinations like Varanasi, Tirupati, Prayagraj, Ayodhya and Shirdi continue to see long-term growth with Gen Z participation rising sharply, particularly through bus and train travel.

items.statement: Early signs of organic inbound travel from Middle East/Southeast Asia, aided by e-tourist visa expansion to 211 countries
items.quote: We are beginning to see early signs of organic inbound travel, particularly from the Middle East and Southeast Asia, which will be further aided by the government's expansion of the e-tourist visa scheme to 211 countries.

items.statement: Bus passenger segment grew 33% YoY to 6.73M; revenue up 47% to ₹75.6 cr
items.quote: The passenger segment grew 33% Y-o-Y to 6.73 million with revenue from operations up 47% to INR75.6 crores.

items.statement: Bus GTV rose 36% to ₹671 cr; compounding 40-50% YoY
items.quote: We have scaled it to over INR2,400 crores of GTV in the last 12 months, representing nearly 6x growth, and it continues to compound at 40% to 50% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Flights GTV grew 22% YoY; revenue grew 49% YoY despite December disruptions
items.quote: Despite the severity of the disruptions, our flights business grew faster than the overall market, with flights GTV growing at 22% and flight revenue growing at 49% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Train bookings grew 8.8% YoY to 26.12M segments; GTV up 15% to ₹2,095.5 cr
items.quote: In trains, we booked 26.12 million train segments, up 8.8% Y-o-Y. GTV was INR2,095.5 crores, up 15%.

items.statement: Flights GTV now nearly equals train GTV; trains still 43% of GTV and 35% of contribution margin
items.quote: The train segment remains an important pillar of ixigo's multimodal strategy, accounting for 43% of GTV and 35% of contribution margin and growing in the mid-teens. Our leadership here is underpinned by deep product innovation, AI-driven complexity management and a strong peace of mind stack for train travellers.

items.statement: Bus contribution margin percentage at 45% (down 1% YoY)
items.quote: Contribution margin was down 1% to INR34 crores and at a 45% contribution margin percentage.

items.statement: Flight disruptions in December (12 days) caused ~₹2 cr EBITDA impact; customer-friendly policies mitigated losses
items.quote: The disruption in the flight operations during December arising from operational challenges faced by a leading operator, including the impact of loss booking and cancellation, would have resulted in an approximate adverse impact of INR2 crores on our EBITDA in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Bus safety inspections led to supplier grounding in November, limiting marketing impact
items.quote: It would have had a bigger impact if it was not for the additional safety inspections that led to the grounding of some suppliers in November.

items.statement: 25% of preferential issue proceeds earmarked for inorganic growth (AI/travel tech/talent); Investment Committee to evaluate high-impact opportunities
items.quote: We will continue to deploy capital only into high-impact opportunities that align with our strategy and offer clear synergies, whether through AI, travel tech or exceptional talent that fits into our long-term vision.

items.statement: Flight business growth driven by organic channels
items.quote: The fastest-growing channel for growth on all 3 lines of businesses are organic for us.

items.statement: Organic growth would have been faster if not for inorganic factors
items.quote: if we were declaring just organic, the growth would have been faster, way faster.

items.statement: Kumbh event contributed mid-to-high single-digit GTV in Q4 last year
items.quote: Last year, Kumbh was a mid to high single-digit GTV contributor. So in the Q4 numbers for last year.

items.statement: Hotel business in build-out phase, not yet at product-market fit
items.quote: we are still in the build-out phase and we're still in the product market fit phase.

items.statement: No significant unique inventory focus in hotels; prioritizing product-market fit
items.quote: in terms of very, very unique inventory, as of now, that's not really something that we will be able to focus on because right now, our bigger focus area is on creating product market fit.

items.statement: Hotel business penetration currently ~20%, expects growth via superior product experience
items.quote: Hotel category is at 20s penetration. So you want to grow more new users from it. So these are areas where we'll not be shy of investing, yes.

items.statement: Pricing is a lever for customer acquisition, but not the only one; discounts used to scale product
items.quote: Pricing will always be a lever, not the only lever, though, okay? But like I said, if you are looking at building a great product, I mean, if customers don't come, for example, if somebody has never booked a flight on ixigo, they would never understand the kind of post-booking experience that we

items.statement: Singapore subsidiary set up for overseas investments in travel, tech, or AI-adjacent areas
items.quote: the Singapore subsidiary in some sense would be a channel for the overseas investment that we would be doing. And as we've said, and we've defined how and why we would be doing the investments through the past, it's that channel that we are looking for and setting up for.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected in 3-5 years, not guided quarterly
items.quote: the answer to this question will be more obvious, let's say, in a 3 to 5 year time frame rather than, let's say, 6 to 12-month time frame, that's the way to think about it, which is why we are not guiding on any sort of margins formally to the market.

items.statement: Hotel direct supply addition via channel managers, not people-intensive; scaling contingent on product-market fit
items.quote: it's not a people-intensive way of adding the supply that we are sort of pursuing as a strategy. The reason is that till the product market fit that Rajnish talked about at this point, where we want to be in product market fit, on what you see versus what you get.

items.statement: No plans for localized travel platforms for Indian diaspora in Middle East
items.quote: At this point, we don't have any, but as and when we have any specific investments or acquisitions to announce, obviously, we'll come to the market with them.

items.statement: Zee Marathi achieved 33.6% market share; South network share at 17.7%; Zee Bangla regained leadership in East.
items.quote: For Zee Marathi, the new content slate has resonated strongly with the consumers across Maharashtra, enabling us to achieve a market share of 33.6%.

items.statement: Content inventory advances and deposits declined by INR 1.2 billion over the last 9 months to INR 69.3 billion as of December 2025.
items.quote: Overall, our content inventory advances and deposits stood at INR 69.3 billion, down by INR 1.2 billion over the last 9 months.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR 21.8 billion as of December 2025, comprising cash, fixed deposits, and liquid mutual funds.
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of December 2025 stood at INR 21.8 billion, comprising of cash of INR 5.0 billion, fixed deposits of INR 7.0 billion and investments in liquid mutual funds of INR 9.8 billion.

items.statement: Deferred further FCCB drawdowns; will not raise more until full visibility on deployment of proceeds.
items.quote: We have deferred the next drawdowns. And we have said it very clearly before also unless we have full visibility on the deployment of those proceeds, we are not going to go for any drawdowns.

items.statement: Headcount rationalization done across the company to remove overlaps between linear and digital businesses; operating at optimized cost structure.
items.quote: There were certain overlaps in linear and digital businesses, which made certain positions redundant. So that was the genesis of the restructuring.

items.statement: Star arbitration hearing adjourned to July 2026; verdict timing uncertain.
items.quote: the next hearing will be somewhere in July. So, I think that's all we can express on this call right now.

items.statement: Revised pricing agreement with a telco player and syndication revenues aided digital revenue growth this quarter.
items.quote: The revenue growth was aided by syndication revenues and revised pricing agreement with a telco player during this quarter, along with improved advertising revenues.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization declining due to low capitalization in recent years and amortization of past tech centre investments in Bengaluru.
items.quote: This has been because in the last few years, our capitalization has not been very high. So, it is just a normal amortization as per the policy. And it is just that the rate of our addition to fixed assets has not been very high.

items.statement: Advertising recovery dependent on FMCG spending pickup and GST cut benefits, which are not yet fully visible.
items.quote: we are yet to see the full benefits of GST cut and a sustained pickup in FMCG advertising spend towards brand building.

items.statement: ESG score of 51 out of 100 in Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment, ranking Zee among top 5% of global media and entertainment players.
items.quote: progress we have made in our ESG journey, which is also reflected in our score of 51 out of 100 in the Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment in the media and entertainment sector. This ranks Zee amongst the top 5% of global players in this sector.

items.statement: Targets Rs 6,000 crore revenue in FY27 from existing assets; Rs 6,500 crore if US tariffs resolve
items.quote: So, in a nutshell, we can hit Rs. 6,500 crores next year. But Rs. 6,000 crores is very visible and with better margins.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 revenue around Rs 1,475 crore, ~14-15% sequential growth
items.quote: I think going forward, January to March looks like again a 20% turnover growth increase from the previous quarter. I think we are looking at 14%, 15%.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA per wheel of Rs 270 in Q4 FY26; aims for Rs 300 eventually
items.quote: So, I think Rs. 270 should not be far. We are hoping that in the fourth quarter we will hit Rs. 270.

items.statement: FY26 capex Rs 225-250 crore, part of multi-year Bhuj project
items.quote: FY 2026 will be around Rs. 225 crores to Rs. 250 crores. Part of CAPEX spend will share for the next year.

items.statement: Aluminum wheel capacity to reach 5 million annualized by March 2026; Bhuj adds 1.2M wheels and 0.6M knuckles by Diwali 2026
items.quote: So, it will be 6.2 for aluminum wheels. And it will be 1.1 for knuckles.

items.statement: CV and tractor OTR segments at 100% utilization; aluminum wheels at ~4.6-4.7M annualized, targeting 5M by March
items.quote: We are totally sold out in the CV segment. We are totally sold out in the tractor OTR segment. We are completely 100% running there.

items.statement: Aluminum order book sold out for next two years; strong domestic order visibility across tractor, aluminum wheels, CV
items.quote: Our entire order book for aluminum is sold out for the next two years.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel rose to Rs 260 in Q3 from Rs 240 previous quarter; driven by higher utilization and value-added mix
items.quote: And the margin per wheel has gone up, from Rs. 240 in the last quarter, it has gone to Rs.260 this quarter, right?

items.statement: Expects margin improvement in Q4 as conversion costs decline with higher utilization
items.quote: With the higher utilization, our conversion costs are coming down, our fixed costs are coming down. So you will naturally see an increase in margins in the month of January to March.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across CV (16% YoY), tractor (12-13%), aluminum wheels, two-wheelers; export demand subdued due to US tariffs
items.quote: Despite sluggish demand in the export market, we delivered strong performance supported by healthy domestic demand.

items.statement: Europe now 58% of export revenue; expects European OEM business to double in FY27
items.quote: Europe has emerged as a key growth market for us and now accounts for over 58% of our export revenue. We expect this diversified mix to remain intact throughout this year.

items.statement: US steel wheel exports down Rs 300-400 crore annually; could recover Rs 500 crore if tariffs resolve and competitors face duties
items.quote: Our steel business of exports has been compromised to the extent of Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 400 crores from the American market.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through is absolute for aluminum (quarterly) and steel (quarterly); no margin impact
items.quote: Once for all, I want to clarify that raw material is a pass-through. So every three months there is a change in aluminum prices that is set up by the customer based on the previous three months rates.

items.statement: Negotiated price increases with two key passenger car customers; effective next year
items.quote: We have negotiated with two important customers of ours. And they have given us a price increase, and it is getting reflected slowly every year. Next year is going to be more effective.

items.statement: Alloy wheels 37% of revenue, 20% of volume in 9M FY26; aluminum knuckle revenue ~Rs 54 crore, targeting Rs 80-90 crore by year-end
items.quote: Alloy wheels have been a key driver, contributing approximately 37% to the total revenue and 20% in the volume terms.

items.statement: Expanding aluminum knuckle customer base beyond EVs into ICE; onboarding new OEMs in Europe for knuckles and wheels
items.quote: Our focus remains on broadening the customer base by onboarding additional OEMs where we are seeing encouraging progress.

items.statement: Thailand and Vietnam aluminum wheel exports under US investigation for circumvention; could benefit India if duties imposed
items.quote: Our competition in Thailand and in Vietnam is coming under investigation for circumventing duties. So if these two things happen, that those guys get caught up in that trap and suddenly tariffs with India open up, then we can hit Rs. 500 crores additional revenue from America.

items.statement: Bhuj capex funded by mix of debt and internal accruals; robust EBITDA accretion expected
items.quote: It will be a mix of debt as well as our internal accruals. So we foresee a very robust EBITDA accretion going with this fourth quarter and the whole next year.

items.statement: Tractor industry growth 12-13% YoY; company fully sold out in tractor OTR segment
items.quote: Tractors again have been showing us a 12% to 13% growth rate.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty persists; resolution expected in 3-6 months; export revenue at risk until resolved
items.quote: We are hoping by end of March, things should happen. And so next financial year is a clear home run for us once these tariffs are removed.

items.statement: Aluminum wheel greenfield capex cost high industry-wide; payback ~7 years on conservative assumptions
items.quote: We are getting our payback in seven years. Seven years we are getting our money back.

items.statement: Investing in digitalization and AI to be future-ready within one year
items.quote: We are investing money in digitalization. We are investing money in AI, and we will be very future-ready in the next one year.

items.statement: Government infrastructure focus creating robust multi-year project pipeline across all regions driving sustained cement demand
items.quote: Government's focus on infrastructure is translating into a robust pipeline of new projects nationwide with several marquee investments announced across every region, translating into solid demand.

items.statement: All-India cement demand growth expected at 9-10% for Q3 FY26 and 6.5-7% for 9M FY26
items.quote: Don't hold me to it, but we would expect anywhere between 9% to 10% all-India demand.

items.statement: 8-9 million tons capacity addition in Q4 FY26, 12 million tons in FY27, balance in FY28 for 22 million ton expansion phase
items.quote: So, we should have approximately 8 to 9 million tons more coming in this quarter. And the balance,12 million tons in fiscal '27 and then balance remaining will be in '28.

items.statement: 9-month capex at INR7,000-7,200 crores, Q4 FY26 capex INR2,000-2,500 crores, full year FY26 around INR9,500-10,000 crores
items.quote: INR7,000 crores to INR7,200 crores is 9 months and yes INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores will get spent in this quarter. So anywhere around INR9,500 crores, INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Kesoram efficiency capex INR263 crores spent of INR382 crores committed; India Cements INR144 crores spent of INR601 crores committed; benefits from January-March 2027
items.quote: At Kesoram, we have already spent INR263 crores, out of the commitment of about INR382 crores. At India Cements, we have committed already INR601 crores and spent INR144 crores on the program.

items.statement: Cables and wires project INR500 crores orders placed, INR197 crores spent, 30% team onboard, civil work started, launch targeted October-December 2026 quarter
items.quote: About INR500 crores worth of orders have already been placed. We have spent INR197 crores. 30% of the planned team is already onboard, civil work has started, and we are on schedule to see the launch of our product in the October-December '26 quarter.

items.statement: Efficiency improvement program delivered INR86/ton last year, expected to cross INR100/ton this fiscal year; lead distance improved to 363 km from 400 km target, clinker factor 1.49 vs 1.54 target
items.quote: Last year, full year, on those quantified measurable targets, we have delivered INR86 per ton. My guess is we should be crossing INR100 mark on those efficiency improvement programs in this financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA per ton expected to be significantly better than Q3's INR916; employee cost increase due to annual increments and new plant additions
items.quote: To your second question, we will do much better than what we did this quarter. I don't want to get into any specific number.

items.statement: Cement prices improving across all segments with growing demand; INR3-4/ton naked realization increase and INR6-8/ton price increase vs Q3 average; cost pass-through expected for pet coke, coal, labor code, rupee depreciation
items.quote: I think we are roughly INR3 to INR4 on a naked cement realization basis up. If naked cement realization is up INR3 to INR4, prices are up , it's somewhere around INR6 to INR8.

items.statement: FY26 capacity 198-199 million tons, FY27 adds 12 million tons, FY28 reaches 235 million tons
items.quote: '26 should be 198, 199 and then 12 more million tons in towards '27, yes.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity utilization expected above 90% of existing installed capacity
items.quote: January-March quarter, God willing, we will operate at more than 90% of our existing installed capacity.

items.statement: Kesoram brand conversion at 69% (crossed 70% currently), India Cements at 58% (crossed 55% currently); full rebranding targeted by June 2026
items.quote: Brand conversion at Kesoram having reached 69% in December '25. And today, if we speak, it must have crossed further. India Cements has already crossed 58% at the end of December '25.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA/ton at INR600 in Q3 vs INR755 in Q2; target INR1,000 exit Q4 FY27 through brand conversion, price improvement, efficiency capex and capacity utilization
items.quote: Balance almost 40% or 45% of brand conversion has to be completed and prices are going up in the southern markets as well. Further, as I called out, the capex program has begun for efficiency improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA at 1.08x; target 0.8-0.9x by end FY26; all growth funded through internal accruals
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we are at 1.08x net debt EBITDA. I believe and I'm very confident that we'll reach the mark of 1x and be in 0.8, 0.9x net debt EBITDA by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: India Cements non-core land parcels sale expected to generate minimum INR500 crores; INR200-250 crores realized so far; Indonesian coal mining company sold
items.quote: I would expect further generation of up to INR500 crores minimum, which we should be able to get.

items.statement: Clinker conversion factor target 1.54 by mid FY27-FY28, currently at 1.49; green power share target 60% by FY27 or H1 FY28 from current 41%
items.quote: We have taken a target of clinker conversion factor of 1.54. We are moving on that direction. In 1.54, we have reached INR1.49.

items.statement: Lead distance reduced to 363 km vs 375 km target (25 km reduction from 400 km base)
items.quote: We have already reached 363 kilometers.

items.statement: Industry capacity additions will be absorbed by strong demand; no pricing pressure expected if demand remains robust
items.quote: The reason I talked about all the demand footprint and demand new initiatives, I think cement will easily get absorbed. And if the demand remains strong, we will not see any problem in prices.

items.statement: South India witnessing large institutional demand from Amaravati city project, IT complexes, data centers, highways; young IT population driving housing and social infrastructure demand
items.quote: South is witnessing large institutional demand, the Am ravati City project, which is going at its breakneck pace, the IT complexes. Complexes which are coming up, data centers which are coming up.

items.statement: Input cost risks from pet coke/coal prices, new labor code impact, rupee depreciation; dollar movement uncertainty affects Q4 cost outlook
items.quote: There have been cost increases in the cost of pet coke and coal, new labor code will have its own impact, rupee depreciation. All these will have an impact on the cement industry.

items.statement: Acquisition opportunities highly opportunistic; would examine if they come to table; nothing currently in progress
items.quote: It's highly opportunistic. We would love to examine opportunities if they come to the table.

items.statement: Industry demand growth guidance 7-8% for next 4-5 years remains intact; Q4 FY26 demand robust but 9-10% may be optimistic due to high base
items.quote: That remains. That remains, Shravan.

items.statement: Other operating income increased INR88 crores sequentially due to incentive transitions (Dhar line 1 exhausted, Dhar line 2 kicked in) and volume-market mix changes
items.quote: Case in point, our Dhar line 1 got exhausted, whatever was the balancing quantum of money left and Dhar 2 kicked in.

items.statement: Early-stage construction products like cement and steel performed well in Q2 and expected to perform strongly in Q3, increasing project pipeline for tiling
items.quote: Early-stage products like cement and steel did well in quarter 2 and are expected to perform strongly in quarter 3 also. This is good news for us as it increases the project pipeline for tiling.

items.statement: Industry exports estimated to grow 8% over last year for 8 months FY26 till November 2025, helping divert capacities from domestic to international markets
items.quote: Data till November '25 suggests that for 8 months FY '26, exports are estimated to grow by 8% over last year. This should help by diverting capacities from domestic to international markets.

items.statement: Full impact of cement and steel demand on tile demand expected to start coming in second half of calendar year 2026, progressively improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: I think it would take, say 3, 4 quarters for it to start playing up. So I think middle of this calendar year -- and it will progressively keep improving quarter-on-quarter, but I think the full impact should start coming in, in the second half of this calendar year.

items.statement: Manufacturing cost reduced 4.5% on like-for-like basis after normalizing for product mix and energy prices; gross margins sustained at mid to high 30s
items.quote: A sharp focus on operational efficiency has led to a 4.5% reduction in the manufacturing cost on a like-for-like basis after normalizing for product mix and energy prices.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA increased 35% year-on-year to INR10.8 crores; PBT rose to INR4.7 crores from INR1.4 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Q3 FY '26 EBITDA increased by a robust 35% year-on-year to INR10.8 crores. Profit before tax rose to INR4.7 crores compared to INR1.4 crores in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA stood at INR26.1 crores, up 25% year-on-year; PBT improved to INR8 crores from INR0.2 crores in corresponding period last year
items.quote: For the 9 months ended FY '26, EBITDA stood at INR26.1 crores, marking a 25% increase year-on-year basis. PBT improved significantly to INR8 crores from INR0.2 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle remains healthy at 31 days, in line with December 2024 levels
items.quote: The working capital cycle remains healthy at 31 days, in line with December '24 levels.

items.statement: Company is virtually debt-free on a net basis with net debt of just INR0.1 crores, reflecting strong liquidity and cash flow
items.quote: Importantly, the company is now virtually debt-free on a net basis with a net debt of just INR0.1 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization in the 65%-odd range, similar to last quarter
items.quote: So current utilizations are similar to the last quarter. It's in the 65%-odd range only.

items.statement: 61% of sales from vitrified segment; GVT alone contributes 44% of sales during Q3, higher than previously
items.quote: 61% of our sales today comes from vitrified segment, which is higher than what it was previously, while GVT alone contributes 44% of our sales during Q3.

items.statement: Focus shifting to high-end GVT with more surface finishes; entry-level GVT facing price competition; ceramics declining as GVT manufacturing capacity increased
items.quote: within GVT, now our focus is our high-end GVT. The entry level GVT product is now facing a lot of price competition. So we are moving into the higher end of GVT products, more surface finishes and all

items.statement: Dealer inventory destocking trend played out over last 1.5-2 years; dealers now at comfortable stock levels; primary and secondary sales expected to be in tandem going forward
items.quote: I think over the last 1.5, 2 years, they have brought down their stocks to a level that they are comfortable with. So going forward, I think primary and secondary should be in tandem.

items.statement: Sales team carries target for secondary sale orders generated for dealers; digitized process capturing this on apps; number steadily building up
items.quote: Especially for us for the last 9 months or 1 year, Ashvath, we have been very aggressively pushing our team towards demand generation. So our sales team today carries a target for what is the total secondary sale orders that you have generated for the dealers and given to them, and we have a clear digitized process for capturing that on our apps and all. And that number has been steadily building

items.statement: OBTBs contribute 42% of sales; conscious shift to quality over quantity; closed large number of underperforming OBTBs; focusing on renovating and expanding existing 300+ OBTBs
items.quote: Even today, more than 40% of our sales is coming in from OBTBs -- actually 42% odd. Now your query about number of OBTBs 3 years back and now, so we have made a very conscious shift to start chasing quality versus quantity.

items.statement: No major capacity-enhancing investment planned; company has 42-43 million sqm capacity with associate company; enough spare capacity for next 2-3 years; focus on market building, distribution, brand awareness
items.quote: We have -- I'll just mention another thing that might help you. Anuj had talked about capacity utilization. So we did go through over the last 4 years, a big capacity expansion -- multiple capacity expansion projects. As a company, we now have almost 42 million, 43 million square meters capacity along with are associate company. So we don't -- we do not see any major capacity enhancing investment.

items.statement: Will spend aggressively on TV advertising in FY27, expanding to new regions like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana; also spending on distribution and displays
items.quote: We are going to spend much more aggressively on TV in FY '27 and of course, spend on adding up distribution and displays.

items.statement: Gas prices stable; weighted average basis up only INR0.50 compared to last quarter; no 30% increase as rumored
items.quote: No. So gas prices are pretty much stable. I think on a weighted average basis compared to the last quarter, gas prices are up by INR0.50 only.

items.statement: Morbi pricing declining; company's manufacturing ASPs maintained but Morbi ASPs declined; purchase price from Morbi also declined, benefit passed to dealers
items.quote: And so I think Morbi pricing has been going down as always. I think that's really the norm. And for us also to share our own manufacturing ASPs have been maintained, but our Morbi ASPs have actually declined.

items.statement: Q3 top line increased 3.4% year-on-year; 9M revenue INR474 crores, up 1.1% from last year; growth entirely volume-led from Q2 onwards
items.quote: On the revenue front, quarter 3 top line has increased by 3.4% over last year. For the 9-month period, these figures are INR474 crores, up 1.1% from last year.

items.statement: Volume growth led by core markets North and East; West leading in growth; South growing but muted with some states doing well
items.quote: So the core markets of North and East have continued to do well. We are doing very nicely in Western India also. Actually, that is leading in growth. And South also has -- South, some geographies have started picking up for us nicely.

items.statement: No major capacity addition expected in 2026; only 8-10 plants known to come online through 2026; capacity to remain similar to last 1-2 years
items.quote: Another thing which I spoke about briefly is that we don't see any major capacity addition in 2026. There are hardly another 8, 10 plants which we know of, which will come into play through 2026.

items.statement: Chinese export incentives likely to be removed effective April 1, 2026; should help Indian domestic market compete better with Chinese players
items.quote: Also, one more change, which is anticipated from 1st of April is that there were some export benefits, which Chinese government used to pass on to the exporters. Likely, some of those incentives effective 1st of April will not be there.

items.statement: Tile adhesives moved beyond pilot phase; selling commercially in selected North India markets; national rollout planned next financial year
items.quote: No, no, we are selling now. It's moved beyond the pilot phase. We are selling it commercially.
