items.statement: Slab market has 28-odd manufacturers in Morbi; 3-4 under shutdown; 6-7 new plants expected in CY2026; significant erosion in slab rates; 15mm thickness emerging as granite substitute
items.quote: So there are 28-odd vendors in Morbi doing slabs. A few of them -- I think 3, 4 of them are under shutdown. We expect another 6 or 7 new plants to come in, in calendar year '26 on slabs.

items.statement: No plans to enter slab manufacturing; capex and capacity utilization equation not attractive; already in market as trader
items.quote: Not as a manufacturer. We are already in the market. We don't have plans to get into it as a manufacturer. The kind of capex it takes and the capacity utilization you need to make money, that equation doesn't look very attractive as of now.

items.statement: Digital tools a key differentiator; 9 out of 10 prospective sales hires from tile industry identify Orient Bell as a tech company; 500+ dealers using voice-enabled visualization tool launched May 2019
items.quote: Today, there is a voice-enabled tool, and we have 500-odd dealers who are using it. So all of this helps because these are things which a customer is not able to get from any of the competing brands.

items.statement: Demand conditions stable with building blocks for gradual consumption recovery supported by moderating inflation, GST rationalization, higher MSPs, and healthy crop sowing.
items.quote: We continued to see the building blocks for a gradual recovery in consumption, supported by moderating inflation, improved affordability following the recent GST rate rationalization, which has been transformative, higher MSPs, and a healthy crop sowing season.

items.statement: Expect improved volume growth trajectory in core portfolio while pricing growth moderates; progressive improvement in operating profit growth rates.
items.quote: We aim to sustain the volume growth momentum even as pricing growth is likely to moderate over the course of the next few quarters. With input cost easing and margin pressure subsiding, we expect progressive improvement in operating profit growth rates over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Target mid-teens operating profit growth and 150-200 bps operating margin expansion.
items.quote: We could try for more, and at least we would strive for improving the operating margin by about 150-200 basis points.

items.statement: Copra prices down 25-30% from peak; Parachute will pass benefit to consumers in coming months via single price cut after March-April visibility.
items.quote: With correction having set in and copra prices down by around 25% to 30% from peak levels, the brand will be passing on the benefit to the consumer in the coming months, as and when we believe it is the right time to do it.

items.statement: No immediate Parachute price cut; will take one correction after March-April when copra trajectory firms up; may use consumer offers interim.
items.quote: We are still awaiting to get a firm handle on how the copra price trajectory will move, which we will get by March-April, and then take correction in one go, rather than taking in multiple steps, because if you take pricing correction in multiple steps, it disturbs the trade rhythm.

items.statement: VAHO value share at all-time high ~30% MAT; double-digit growth trajectory expected near-to-medium term.
items.quote: Our value share on MAT basis stands at an all-time high of nearly 30%, showing considerable progress towards premiumization of the mix and bridging the gap between volume and value share, along with our intended lines and long-term aspirations.

items.statement: Foods portfolio paused growth to rectify low-profitability SKUs; confident of resuming accelerated organic growth in next two quarters.
items.quote: We remain very bullish on value-added foods and nutra opportunity in India, and our strategy to invest in fewer, bigger, better plays in terms of our portfolio approach. That being said, we are confident of resuming the accelerated growth trajectory in our organic food business over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Strategic investment in 4700BC at INR 140 cr ARR; target 3x ARR in three years; synergies with True Elements for cost and GTM.
items.quote: It is clocking at about INR 140 crores ARR in the last three months. We see tremendous potential for the brand to scale its ARR to 3x in the next three years.

items.statement: Premium Personal Care portfolio to exit FY26 at ARR INR 350+ cr; Digital-First portfolio to exit FY26 at ARR INR 1,000+ cr; target 2.5x FY24 ARR next year.
items.quote: In Premium Personal Care, the portfolio comprising Serums, Male Grooming, and Skincare grew in double digits and is expected to exit the year at an ARR of INR 350+ crores. In addition, the Digital-First portfolio is expected to exit FY '26 with an ARR of INR +1,000 crores.

items.statement: Digital-First portfolio target double-digit EBITDA margin by end of FY27.
items.quote: We are on track to reach 2.5x of FY '24 ARR next year, and we are making concerted efforts to move to double-digit EBITDA margin in the Digital-First portfolio by end of FY '27.

items.statement: Project SETU ~30% complete; 3-5 year project to deepen rural coverage and expand urban channels (chemist, cosmetic, specialty food).
items.quote: Project SETU has continued to strengthen our distribution fundamentals, execution capabilities, and the coverage expansion remains firmly on track, led by deeper presence in upgraded towns and pan-India rural scale-up. We will now commence our initiatives on targeted expansion in urban channels, such as chemist, cosmetic, and specialty food outlets.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick commerce leading growth; traditional trade showing clear improvement from consistent investments.
items.quote: Among channels, while e-commerce and quick commerce were leading growth drivers, we saw a clear improvement in traditional trade, marking the outcome of consistent investments and targeted actions over the last 2 years.

items.statement: At least one competitor in coconut oil now following rational pricing model, avoiding negative gross margins.
items.quote: Number three, which is also gives us hope that at least one of our competitors is being extremely rational on pricing, because we also faced, as you know, irrational pricing from two competitors in the past, and now at least one of them is following a rational pricing model.

items.statement: International business robust broad-based growth; Bangladesh steady core and new franchises; Vietnam and South Africa double-digit constant currency growth; MENA strong; NCD accelerated.
items.quote: Bangladesh led from the front, supported by a steady core business and a scale -up of new franchises like shampoos. Vietnam and South Africa bounced back to deliver do uble-digit constant currency growth, driven by targeted initiatives. MENA continued to deliver strong performance in key franchises across both the Gulf region and Egypt . The NCD business also delivered accelerated growth

items.statement: Bangladesh macro uncertainties monitored; business resilient with 8% growth in Q2 despite grim conditions.
items.quote: Even in Quarter 2, when the issues were quite grim in terms of the, it was in August that this thing happened. That quarter, we grew by 8%. So, we have taken steps out there, and we don't see any reason to be extremely concerned at this moment in time in terms of delivering business.

items.statement: Supply chain efficiencies and AI-based forecasting enable far thinner pipelines; changeover much faster vs 8-12 weeks previously.
items.quote: The big change that has happened is that we work with far, far thinner pipelines because of our supply chain efficiencies and our AI-based forecasting models. So, therefore, we are compared to, say, five years ago and all that, that the changeover, which used to take 8 weeks to 12 weeks, especially in rural, this is going to be much faster.

items.statement: Consolidated high single-digit revenue growth expected for FY26; India business to hold normative EBITDA margins in Q4 FY26; GAUM to deliver double-digit revenue and profit growth for FY26; Indonesia recovery expected from FY27
items.quote: For the year, we remain confident of achieving high single -digit revenue growth at a consolidated level. Our India business is expected to deliver continued growth performance while holding normative EBITDA margins in the coming quarter. GAUM continues to perform well and deliver on its stated objectives of double-digit revenue and profit growth for the year.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin annual range guided at 24-26% for FY26; management expects margins to stay within this range and not exceed it due to negative mix from fast-growing categories
items.quote: I would be surprised if we exceed this 24% to 26% range. This is also an annual range; on a quarter it may go up and down. The annual range of 24% to 26% is roughly where we will be is what I think.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin at 24.8% in Q3 FY26 driven by cost savings (media, supply chain, blend flex), favourable input costs, calibrated pricing and operating leverage; structural savings to persist
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at a healthy 24.8%, supported by favourable input costs, disciplined cost management, calibrated pricing actions, and improved operating leverage. I think the few quarters that we had of margin challenges is probably behind us.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 16% with margins at 21.6% in Q3 FY26; Indonesia profitability improved ~100 bps YoY; GAUM EBITDA grew 18%
items.quote: Revenues grew 9% in INR terms, underpinned by a healthy 7% underlying volume growth. EBITDA expanded by 16%, with margins reaching 21.6%. Our net profit before exceptionals grew by 14% underlying the quality and sustainability of our earnings growth.

items.statement: Indonesia delivered stable 5% underlying volume growth led by shampoo, hair colour, baby care with market share gains across categories; revenue flattish due to distribution changes
items.quote: The gy business delivered a stable UVG of 5% led by shampoo, hair colour, baby care and with market share gains across all categories. Revenue was flattish, adjusting for the one -off changes in distribution adjustment.

items.statement: GAUM (Africa, USA, Middle East) sales grew 19% in INR terms with strong performance in hair fashion and air fresheners; aer pocket launch resonating well
items.quote: Our Africa, U.S.A. and Middle East GAUM business delivered outstanding results, wi th sales growth of 19% in INR terms. EBITDA grew 18%, led by strong performance in hair fashion and air fresheners.

items.statement: Home Care grew 12% value led by air fresheners, fabric care, household insecticides (RNF formulations); Personal Care recovered 7% with soaps improving post-GST cut; incense sticks grew fast with 30% price hike and no volume slowdown
items.quote: delivered 12% value growth led by strong performance in air fresheners and fabric care alongside continued market share gains in household insecticide, driven by our superior RNF based formulations. We continue to expect similar share gains going forward. Personal Care witnessed a meaningful recovery, growing 7% with soaps demonstrating a positive trajectory, supported by improving affordability f

items.statement: Fast-growing categories (air care, laundry liquids, incense sticks, EDP/perfumes) growing at 30%+ with large TAMs; hair colour and non-mosquito HI growing double-digits; soaps expected 4-6% value growth long-term
items.quote: The three big categories that have been growing very fast for us have been air care, laundry liquid, and incense sticks. These are the three that have really and they're now becoming all of them are material size and rapid growth. All of them have very large TAMs. I think that's and there's a fourth one that seems to be emerging by the way, it's still not large enough, which is perfumes, EDP.

items.statement: Muuchstac acquisition completed 10 Nov 2024; business ~INR 70 cr, men's face wash market ~INR 1,000 cr growing 20%; targeting #2 position; Park Avenue (Raymond) acquisition progressing reasonably, EDP segment exploding to ~INR 100 cr
items.quote: I am pleased to confirm that our acquisition of Muuchstac was successfully completed on 10th November, with operations now fully live and performance on plan. This strategic addition strengthens our portfolio in the fast -growing men's face wash segment and positions us well to capture emerging opportunities in this space.

items.statement: Pet food test market in Tamil Nadu showing mixed results; market share lower than hoped; plant ready in Nashik; building capabilities (kennel, manufacturing, sales team, vet program); long-term commitment, slow burn for few years
items.quote: We basically launched a test market in Tamil Nadu and as we speak, we have got a plant ready now in Nashik, which is ready to go. I think in Tamil Nadu, our results have been mixed. We've had some success in terms of consumer traction, distribution, etc. But I don't think we're still at a position where we can say we've got the mix 100% right.

items.statement: Incense sticks: 30% weighted average price increase since launch with no volume slowdown, margins now good; soaps: blend flex savings from vegetable oil vs fossil fuel price shifts; media savings from new agency and better internal planning
items.quote: Yes, in incense sticks, we have taken a weighted average price increase of 30% since we launched, and we are seeing no slowdown in our volume growth. So now our margins are pretty good actually in incense sticks.

items.statement: Cost savings driving margin improvement: significant media savings (new agency, better GRP efficiency), supply chain savings (new factories), blend flex in soaps and detergents; 50% of other expense reduction from savings, rest phasing
items.quote: We've had an unusually high year in terms of cost savings. I think we've had very significant savings in media cost. So actually, while our ATL looks optically lower, the number of GRPs that we are spending in the market is actually higher. And I think , we made a big decision to change to a very large new media house, and that has a significant media savings.

items.statement: Household Insecticides: RNF molecule driving share gains in all 4 segments (incense sticks, electrics, aerosols, coils); overall HI volume growth mid-single digit, inching to high single digit; volatility +/-5% per quarter
items.quote: I think the RNF won't change the volatility of HI results because the volatility of HI results depends on the volatility of seasonality. It will change the mean from a business that was practically not growing. I think it is going to go and as our incense sticks business becomes bigger and bigger, and that business is now quite a profitable business. And we're having good success in market share i

items.statement: Soap volume growth positive in Q3 but below expectations; GST transition and cold winter impacted Oct-Nov; December strong; long-term soap value growth expected 4-6% with low single-digit volume and pricing
items.quote: I think it's a good question. I expect soap value to grow at between 4% and 6% in the long-term basis, low single-digit volume growth and low single-digit pricing as well. That's what I expect in soaps.

items.statement: Margins sensitive to sharp oil price increases (>15%); if oil spikes, margins may take 1-2 quarters to recover as company won't cut media spending; pass-through faster on price drops than hikes
items.quote: I would say that if there is a very sharp increase in oil prices again, and when I say very sharp, it has to be greater than 15 -odd percent, then we will take another quarter or two to recover the margins. We won't react in the short term by cutting media just to cover up some margins optically.

items.statement: Indonesia near-term volatility due to Labaran (Ramzan) date shift; competitive intensity peak behind but market remains competitive; currency fluctuations affect GAUM reported growth
items.quote: This quarter, again, in Indonesia, optically, the results may not great because of the change in dates of Labaran, which is Ramzan for them. But the underlying 4%, 5% volume seems to be back, and it will follow in price soon.

items.statement: GST reduction on soaps improving affordability and supporting volume recovery; transition impacted Oct-Nov stock clearance, benefits visible from December
items.quote: Personal Care witnessed a meaningful recovery, growing 7% with soaps demonstrating a positive trajectory, supported by improving affordability following the GST reduction and stable commodity prices.

items.statement: Indonesia competitive intensity peak (6 months of high pricing competition) appears behind; market remains competitive but stabilizing; GAUM facing currency volatility but structural volume growth strong
items.quote: I think the peak of competitive intensity is indeed behind us. It continues to be competitive like every other part, but there was a period of 6 months of very highly competitive activity on pricing which does seem to be a little bit behind.

items.statement: Other expenses in India down ~6% YoY in Q3; 50% from structural savings (media, supply chain, other cost lines), 50% from phasing between quarters
items.quote: I would say 50% of it would be attributable to savings. There have been savings in other cost lines and part of it has to do with phasing. And then in a quarter, there is some phasing which happens quarter -to-quarter on cost, but we have managed to kind of save on to some of the other expenses.

items.statement: Media function: creative insourced, media buying bolstered in-house with technology, still working with Group M; advertising function internal
items.quote: I think we made a presentation on insourcing the creative function. The media buying, we have actually bolstered our team in -house and there's a lot of use of technology. So, one reason for the reduction in media cost is the agency. Another reason is far better internal planning, but our media function is not an in -house function. We continue to work with Group M, and o ur advertising function i

items.statement: Litigation costs (Strength of Nature class action) ~INR 23 cr in quarter; legal expenses likely to continue for few quarters as suit progresses
items.quote: I mean there is, some of the costs are getting incurred in terms of legal expenses, which are being incurred. We will have to see how the suit progresses. But yes, it's likely to kind of continue for a few quarters.

items.statement: NIM expected to be in the range of 2.45% to 2.50% even if further repo rate cuts happen
items.quote: So, even if further reduction in Repo happens, we presume that our NIM will be in the range of 2.45 to 2.50.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 10-11% already surpassed at 13.59% and will be maintained
items.quote: Regarding credit growth, sir, you have told we have given a guidance of 10% to 11%, but already we are crossing 13.59%, and we see that going ahead this will be maintained.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance of 9-10% already surpassed at near 13% and will be maintained in Q4
items.quote: And on the deposit side also, we have given a guidance of 9% to 10%. We are already near 13%, and we see that it will be maintained in the 4th Quarter also.

items.statement: NIM contracted by 2 bps in Q3 due to 6 bps yield compression on advances partly offset by 4 bps deposit cost reduction
items.quote: Regarding margins, our NIM contracted by 2 basis points because the yield on advances… because on 5th, there was a reduction in repo by 25 basis points, and about 49% of our advance is Repo linked. So, immediately that transition was happening in those accounts. So, yield on advances contracted by 6 basis points, although the cost of deposit also reduced by 4 basis points, which had a net impact o

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize if no further rate cuts occur due to OMO and swap injecting liquidity and cooling deposit costs
items.quote: With the OMO coming up and the swap being announced, liquidity will be injected, and we see the cost of deposits cooling down further. So yes, if the rate cut doesn't happen, we see that it will stabilize.

items.statement: NIM could improve by 15-20 bps once rate cycle effect settles and deposit repricing catches up with RLLR loan repricing
items.quote: Sir, definitely yes, that will happen as the rate cycle effect settles down. Because now there is always a time lag on passing on the RLLR based loans and the deposit repricing. Once that stabilizes, automatically 15-20 basis point will immediately rise across lenders.

items.statement: RAM credit grew 18.70% YoY to Rs 7.04 lakh crore, driven by retail at 31.37% and MSME at 13.74%
items.quote: Now, more than 13% of our credit growth is driven by RAM credit, which stood at 7.04 lakh crores and grew at 18.70%. The retail credit grew at 31.37% and stood at 2.73 lakh crores. The housing loan grew by 17.58% and stood at 1.21 lakh crores. Vehicle loan also shown fantastic growth. The growth was 26.20% and stood at 25,098 crores. MSME has also shown robust growth of 13.74% and stood at 1.60 la

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio at Rs 2.21 lakh crore growing at 30% YoY, with Agri gold at Rs 1.48 lakh crore and Non-Agri at Rs 72,661 crore
items.quote: Sir, our total gold loan portfolio is 2,21,000 crores. Out of that, Agri gold is 1,48,000 crores. And Non-Agri is 72,661 crores. So, very consciously, we have rolled back the products of gold loan in metropolitan and urban centres because that was the RBI observation. Now, we are totally compliant with it. And our gold loan portfolio is improving at 30% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: SMA-2 down from Rs 21,268 cr to Rs 15,454 cr (2% to 1.30%), SMA-1 down from Rs 11,882 cr to Rs 10,593 cr (1.13% to 0.89%)
items.quote: Sir, our SMA in absolute terms has come down from 43,000 crores to 35,604 crores. The SMA-2 has come down from 21,268 crores to 15,454 crores. And SMA-1 has come down from 11,882 crores to 10,593 crores. So, SMA-2 has come down from 2% to 1.30%. SMA-1 has come down from 1.13% to 0.89%.

items.statement: Fresh slippages in Q3: Agriculture Rs 789 cr, MSME Rs 739 cr, Retail Rs 294 cr, Gold Rs 35 cr; no corporate slippages
items.quote: Yes, sir. In Agriculture, the total slippage is 1,857 crores. 789 is from Agriculture sector. 739 is from MSME. Retail 294 and 35 is from gold. No corporate account has slipped.

items.statement: Written-off book at Rs 66,000 cr; recovery run rate of ~Rs 2,000 cr per quarter to continue in FY27
items.quote: Sir, we have taken a conscious call that it has to be more than the 2,000 crore range, and we are continuously trying to achieve that number. If you see last December also it was 2,008 crores, this year 2,051 crores. Although my total NPA book is falling, we are trying to maintain this recovery ratio.

items.statement: Written-off recoveries split ~50-50 between retail and corporate; retail DWO recovery averages Rs 900-1,000 cr per quarter
items.quote: That is yes. From Retail recovery in DWO is around, on an average. In some quarter it may be more, some quarter it may be less. On an average around 1,000 crores, 900 to 1,000 crores

items.statement: Credit cost improved 25 bps YoY to 0.64%
items.quote: Our credit cost was at 0.64% and improved by 25 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: CET-1 improved 40 bps YoY to 12.37%
items.quote: Our CET-1 stood at 12.37%, which improved by 40 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: CASA grew 9.32% YoY; savings individual >10%, current account 14.92% (impacted by one large transaction)
items.quote: Now, coming to the CASA front also, if you see our savings bank is growing at 8.51%. And saving bank individual is growing more than 10%. So, we are performing better than the peers in savings. Even if you see the current account, it is growing at 14.92%. Only due to one single transaction that has happened previous quarter of 26,000 in current account, that is why Q on Q sub dip is there. But CAS

items.statement: Priority sector lending at 45.25% against 40% norm, enabling continued PSLC income
items.quote: Our total priority sector against 40% norms is now at 45.25%. So there is still some space for offloading PSLC in the fourth quarter to supplement what Mr. Majumdar is saying.

items.statement: PSLC income now sustainable across quarters: Rs 1,240 cr in Q1, Rs 900 cr in Q2, Rs 140 cr in Q3, substantial expected in Q4
items.quote: And this quarter, not only we have earned around 1,240 crores, we have earned 900 crores in the 2 nd Quarter. 3rd Quarter, actually, there is no chance for a PSLC. There also we earned 140 crores. And I assure you, we'll earn a substantial amount in the 4 th Quarter also. So it is the industry; if any regulatory thing has happened, it is only helping us. And it is helping us as a renewed avenue of

items.statement: ECL implementation from April 1, 2027; estimated Rs 10,000 cr total impact (Rs 2,500 cr Stage 2, Rs 2,500 cr NFP, Rs 5,000 cr Stage 1 default rate), amortizable over 4 years at Rs 2,000-2,500 cr per year
items.quote: Coming to ECL, the other parameters madam, it is going to be implemented from 1st April 2027. Now, our bank is making… last year it has made a profit of 17,000 crores. This year, going by the same trend, our profit will be in the range of 17,000 to 20,000 crores. So, in the ECL under Stage 2… because Stage 1 and Stage 3 does not have any much material impact because it is almost similar to IRAC no

items.statement: No pre-emptive ECL provisions being made; quarterly profits sufficient to absorb impact when implemented
items.quote: Sir, we feel we don't need to do any pre-emptive provision before that. That will come from… My quarterly profits will be sufficient at any point in time to absorb that, without hindering business growth and capital position.

items.statement: Annual digital spend ~Rs 1,000 cr (Rs 800-1,000 cr range for last 3 years); AI vertical created with data scientists and Python engineers
items.quote: Around 1,000 crores we are spending annually on digital initiatives. − Mr. S.K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: − For last three years, sir, we have been spending around 1,000 crores, between 800 to 1,000 every year. And I think this year also… we should be able to reap the benefits now

items.statement: Cross-selling through subsidiaries (Canara Robeco, Canara HSBC, Can Fin Homes) generating ~Rs 500 cr income; insurance NFO collected Rs 6,050 cr vs Rs 500 cr target
items.quote: So we are getting substantial benefit out of this. So insurance company in the previous NFO what we have launched, so against the target of 500, we have reaped some 6,050 crores in 15 days' room, what was given. So we are valuing this subsidiary and we are enhancing the value for the customers by cross-selling. So whether it is the Canara Robeco SIPs or mutual fund selling, or it is the insurance

items.statement: No QIP lined up; capital adequacy at 16.5% with Rs 17,000-20,000 cr annual profit sufficient for double-digit growth
items.quote: So QIP, I don't think QIP is now lined up. − Mr. S.K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: − Choksey ji, as you know and you have seen that my capital adequacy is already at 16.5. We are adding around 17,000 to 20,000 profit per annum. So there is no reason… I mean, as of now, we are adequately capitalized to do business, to have a double-digit growth going forward next couple of

items.statement: Deposits from overseas branches reclassified from deposits to borrowings per RBI observation; Rs 33,000 cr reduced in December
items.quote: Sir, there was a RBI observation that overseas branches, that deposits taken from bank were earlier considered as borrowings. Now we… earlier they were considered as deposits. Now we have reclassified as borrowings. And subsequently we have changed in other previous quarters also. That effect has been changed. So 33,000 reclassification has been done… has been reduced. And it ranges from 23,000 fr

items.statement: Treasury income doubled to Rs 3,056 cr in Q3 driven by Rs 2,006 cr listing gains from Canara Robeco (13% stake) and Canara HSBC (14.5% stake) stake sales
items.quote: Sir, in Q3, due to listing profits of Canara Robeco and Canara HSBC… in Canara HSBC we offloaded 14.5% stake, and in Canara Robeco we offloaded 13% stake and could gain 2,006 crores.

items.statement: Standard asset provision of Rs 286 cr includes ~Rs 90 cr for DCCO extension; rest routine
items.quote: Standard asset provision, one is we had to provide for DCCO extension, that some provision of around 80 crores is there… around 90 crores is there. And other than that, I think these are all routine. There is nothing else.

items.statement: Company on track to become debt-free by FY27
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong, and we are on well track to become debt-free by FY27.

items.statement: A&SP spending guided at 6-8% of IMFL revenue
items.quote: We continue to guide for A&SP spending in the range of 6-8% to sustain strong brand visibility and growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve by 125 bps each year for next two years reaching late teens
items.quote: We are going to improve our margin based on our product profile and premiumization happening, by 125 basis points each for next two years, thereby going to late teen kind of margin.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Prestige & Above category, excluding the royalty brands, continued its steady upward trajectory, recording 26% volume growth and 29% value growth, with reali zations improving by 2.8% on year-on-year

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh market share increased from over 15% to 26% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our performance in Andhra Pradesh has been encouraging with our market share increasing from over 15% in Q3 of last year to 26% in the quarter gone by, making us the leading player in the state.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 350 bps YoY to 46.9% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Gross margin during the quarter was 46.9%, representing a 350 bps expansion on year-on-year basis, 290 bps expansion on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Raw material contributed 225 bps of gross margin expansion YoY
items.quote: Raw material accounted for 225 bps of gross margin expansion during the quarter as compared to last year Q3.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps YoY to 17.2% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 300 bps on year-on-year basis to 17.2%.

items.statement: ENA and grain prices expected to stay stable to favorable near-term
items.quote: We remain optimistic that ENA and grain prices will stay stable to favorable in the near-term, providing continued margin support.

items.statement: Scotch prices seeing softening due to oversupply in Scotland
items.quote: We are seeing a price decline in fact in the scotch prices. And there is enough of Scotch which is there. So, we are seeing softening of prices.

items.statement: Premiumization and product mix contributed 125 bps to gross margin expansion YoY
items.quote: It is a combination of softer raw material scenario where we have had an improvement in margin of around 225 basis points, and the premiumization and product mix has been 125 basis points margin improvement.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio revenue expected to reach Rs. 500 crores in FY26 vs Rs. 340 crores last year
items.quote: See, last year we got Rs. 340 crores and this year we should be close to about Rs. 500 crores in revenue terms.

items.statement: On-trade channel now contributes 6-7% of total sales
items.quote: On-trade would be about close to 6%-7% of our total sales now.

items.statement: Exports contribute 5% of volume and 8% of revenue with steady growth
items.quote: Well, as a percentage of the overall business, the volume is about 5% and the revenue is about 8%. And we have been having a steady growth in our export business, both in terms of the luxury portfolio as well as the regular portfolio.

items.statement: Ongoing capex directed towards maintenance and essential capacity optimization
items.quote: Our ongoing capex is largely directed towards maintenance capex and essential capacity optimization.

items.statement: Board approved 100% wholly-owned subsidiary in Scotland to secure malt supply chain
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved setting up a 100% wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company in Scotland. This is in line with our strategy of investing in our Malt capabilities.

items.statement: Scotland subsidiary may evaluate acquiring matured malt inventory or distillery assets opportunistically
items.quote: We will be evaluating, but we are not in a hurry. But we have taken a enabling provision by making company, whether we mature malt out there, we buy directly, or if there is something which is available at a very, very good price, which has the inventory of Scotch, not brand. So, we can look at it, but as of now, nothing is on the cards.

items.statement: Telangana collections improving; old outstanding expected to clear within a month
items.quote: In fact, in the last one to two months, we have got payment out of the old outstanding, and hopefully, the entire old outstanding should be cleared within a month.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by Rs. 209 crores since March 2025
items.quote: Our net debt reduced by Rs. 209 crores since March 2025, driven by improved profitability.

items.statement: Post-debt repayment cash likely to be used for dividend payouts
items.quote: I think depending on the board's decision, but I think mostly it will be used for dividend payouts.

items.statement: On-trade team expanded to 50-70 people over last 1.5 years
items.quote: In fact, in the last one and a half years, we have really beefed up our on-trade team. We have recruited from all the institutions, etc., We have been close to about 50 to 70 people on the on-trade side.

items.statement: Total IMFL volume reached highest-ever 9.75 million cases in Q3 FY26, up 16.7% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, we delivered a strong all-round performance with the highest-ever total IMFL volume of 9.75 million cases, reflecting 16.7% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Royal Ranthambore Whisky grew over 50% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Royal Ranthambore Whisky delivered an outstanding performance with over 50% growth in Q3, driven by strong demand across both civil and CSD channels.

items.statement: Magic Moments Vodka grew 18% volume in Q3 FY26 and crossed Rs. 1,050 crores sales in nine months
items.quote: Magic Moments Vodka continued its strong growth trajectory with 18% volume growth during Q3 and crossed Rs.1,050 crores of sales in the nine-month period.

items.statement: After Dark Whisky grew 40% YoY in Q3 FY26, crossed 2.4 million cases in nine months
items.quote: After Dark Whisky continued to deliver strong performance, recording 40% growth year-on-year in the quarter, crossing 2.4 million cases volume in the nine months.

items.statement: Government infrastructure focus creating robust multi-year project pipeline across all regions driving sustained cement demand
items.quote: Government's focus on infrastructure is translating into a robust pipeline of new projects nationwide with several marquee investments announced across every region, translating into solid demand.

items.statement: All-India cement demand growth expected at 9-10% for Q3 FY26 and 6.5-7% for 9M FY26
items.quote: Don't hold me to it, but we would expect anywhere between 9% to 10% all-India demand.

items.statement: 8-9 million tons capacity addition in Q4 FY26, 12 million tons in FY27, balance in FY28 for 22 million ton expansion phase
items.quote: So, we should have approximately 8 to 9 million tons more coming in this quarter. And the balance,12 million tons in fiscal '27 and then balance remaining will be in '28.

items.statement: 9-month capex at INR7,000-7,200 crores, Q4 FY26 capex INR2,000-2,500 crores, full year FY26 around INR9,500-10,000 crores
items.quote: INR7,000 crores to INR7,200 crores is 9 months and yes INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores will get spent in this quarter. So anywhere around INR9,500 crores, INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton to improve significantly in Q4 FY26 versus Q3 FY26's INR916
items.quote: To your second question, we will do much better than what we did this quarter. I don't want to get into any specific number.

items.statement: Cement prices improving across all segments with INR3-4 per bag naked realization increase and INR6-8 price increase since Q3
items.quote: I think we are roughly INR3 to INR4 on a naked cement realization basis up. If naked cement realization is up INR3 to INR4, prices are up, it's somewhere around INR6 to INR8.

items.statement: Lead distance reduced to 363 km vs 375 km target, clinker factor improved to 1.49 vs 1.54 target, efficiency savings ~INR100/ton expected in FY26
items.quote: We have already reached 363 kilometers. So, it's not only the lead distance, which helps, there is a lot of other initiatives which the team is taking, which helps to take efficiency improvement. Similarly, we have taken a target of clinker conversion factor of 1.54. We are moving on that direction. In 1.54, we have reached INR1.49.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA at 1.08x consolidated, targeting 0.8-0.9x by end of FY26, all growth funded through internal accruals
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we are at 1.08x net debt EBITDA. I believe and I'm very confident that we'll reach the mark of 1x and be in 0.8, 0.9x net debt EBITDA by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Kesoram brand conversion at 69% (Dec'25), India Cements at 58% (Dec'25), cost improvement capex underway: Kesoram INR263/382 crores spent, India Cements INR144/601 crores spent
items.quote: Integration of recent acquisitions is progressing very well with rapid brand transition. Kesoram and India Cements are ahead of the initial plans, with brand conversion at Kesoram having reached 69% in December '25. And today, if we speak, it must have crossed further. India Cements has already crossed 58% at the end of December '25.

items.statement: Cable and wires project: INR500 crores orders placed, INR197 crores spent, 30% team onboard, civil work started, launch targeted Oct-Dec'26
items.quote: Talking about capex, the other initiative, cable and wires is progressing as per plan. About INR500 crores worth of orders have already been placed. We have spent INR197 crores. 30% of the planned team is already onboard, civil work has started, and we are on schedule to see the launch of our product in the October-December '26 quarter as was committed earlier.

items.statement: Premium products share at 36%, RMC at 3% of volumes and growing rapidly, bulk cement increasing, on-site blending declining
items.quote: We missed that. Premium share is 36%.

items.statement: Fly ash and slag sourcing fully secured with mix of long-term, short-term, domestic and import contracts, no limiting factor for clinker factor improvement
items.quote: So, one is there's enough new supply coming up. Power plant capacities are going up, steel plants are coming up. And we have a mix of long-term, short-term domestic and import sourcing, fully secured

items.statement: India Cements non-core asset sales: coal mining company in Indonesia sold, INR200-250 crores realized, targeting additional INR500 crores from land parcels
items.quote: Noncore there are land parcels essentially. We just sold off the coal mining company in Indonesia. The monies have been realized, and that's how you see the debt remaining under control. There are a couple of big land parcels, which we are discussing with potential buyers. I would expect further generation of up to INR500 crores minimum, which we should be able to get.

items.statement: Kesoram EBITDA/ton at ~INR600 in Q3 vs INR755 in Q2, India Cements EBITDA/ton at ~INR400 in Q3 targeting INR1,000 exit by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Would be around INR600 this quarter.

items.statement: Industry demand growth guidance of 7-8% maintained for next 4-5 years, Q4 FY26 demand expected robust but 9-10% may be optimistic
items.quote: That remains. That remains, Shravan.

items.statement: Cost pressures from pet coke, coal, new labor code, rupee depreciation expected to be passed through to prices
items.quote: There have been cost increases in the cost of pet coke and coal, new labor code will have its own impact, rupee depreciation. All these will have an impact on the cement industry. And obviously, there is reason to pass on these cost escalations into prices.

items.statement: Trade ratios strong indicating buoyant rural demand, no depression witnessed, Q4 expected solid
items.quote: Rural demand, simple way to look at rural demand is look at our trade ratios. If our trade ratios remain strong, rural demand is equally buoyant. We are not witnessing any depression in rural demand. Q4 also will be solid is what my expectation is.

items.statement: Industry capacity additions will be absorbed by strong demand, no pricing pressure expected if demand remains robust
items.quote: The reason I talked about all the demand footprint and demand new initiatives, I think cement will easily get absorbed. And if the demand remains strong, we will not see any problem in prices.

items.statement: Operating at >90% capacity utilization in Jan-Mar quarter demonstrating growth in both trade and non-trade markets
items.quote: you will notice that January-March quarter, God willing, we will operate at more than 90% of our existing installed capacity, clearly demonstrating growth in the trade ma rkets as well as non -trade

items.statement: Opportunistic approach to further consolidation, no active deals in progress but will examine opportunities if they arise
items.quote: It's highly opportunistic. We would love to examine opportunities if they come to the table.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to annual compensation hikes and new plant capacity additions, Q2 comparison more appropriate than YoY
items.quote: 916 employee cost going up Y-o-Y because what happens is our annual compensation increases that take place and new plants, of course, new capacity getting added. That is what will reflect in this cost.

items.statement: Not commenting on budget expectations for cement sector
items.quote: The last question first, I won't comment on that.

items.statement: South India to become new North with large institutional demand from Amravati, IT complexes, data centers, highways driving long-term pricing stability
items.quote: I think demand is opening up, and I stand by my statement South will be new north. That doesn't mean North is going away anywhere. North is stronger and stronger. South is witnessing large institutional demand, the Amravati City project, which is going at its breakneck pace, the IT complexes. Complexes which are coming up, data centers which are coming up, which are so cementitious in nature, high

items.statement: Guidance of 18-20% YoY growth and 13.5% ROE for FY27, 14.5% ROE for FY28 remains unchanged
items.quote: As far as the future goes, we continue to remain confident about our guidance of 18% to 20% growth year-on-year, and the 13.5% ROE in '26 -'27 and 14.5% ROE for '27 -'28. That remains unchanged.

items.statement: NIM at 3.27% for Q3, cost of deposits down 10 bps to 6.86%, upward NIM momentum expected to continue till Q1-Q2 FY27
items.quote: NIM continues its upward momentum, clocking 3.27% for the quarter, thanks to reduced cost of deposit, which now stands at 6.86%, that's a 10 basis point drop in the quarter.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced from INR 8,400 cr to INR 4,700 cr, replacing expensive borrowings with lower-cost deposits
items.quote: We had a borrowing, total borrowing of INR 8,400 odd crores. Now it is about INR 4,700 crores. It is just repricing , our ability to get lower cost of deposit by giving away borrowing, which is more expensive, is coming into play very quickly.

items.statement: Credit costs benign at 0.37%, slippage ratio at 3.08% lowest in 18 quarters, GNPA 2.72% lowest in 18 quarters, NNPA 1.1% lowest in 11 quarters
items.quote: Our credit costs are benign at 0.37%, much below the minimum stated goal of 0.45%. What is truly heartening for us is that our slippage ratio for the quarter at 3.08% is the lowest we had in 18 quarters. Our GNPA at 2.72% is the lowest we had, again, strangely in 18 quarters. And our Net NPA at 1.1% is the lowest we had in the last 11 quarters.

items.statement: Recoveries and upgrades at 86% of fresh flow, highest ever; floating provisions not for ECL but to drive NNPA to 1% or below
items.quote: So, if you see, it's a, bounce rate coming down, slippage coming down, gross NPA coming down, net NPA coming down. So, it's all, gross NPA is a net outcome of all these activities that you're doing. So we're very clear. It's not meant for ECL. It's just that, you see our recoveries and upgrades as a percentage of our fresh flow, it is 86%. That

items.statement: Customer advances grew 18.46% YoY, customer deposits grew 19.54% YoY
items.quote: The customer advances have grown Y-o-Y by 18.46%. Customer deposits have grown Y-o-Y by 19.54% and profit after tax has grown Y-o-Y by 22%, despite a onetime impact of INR 26.87 crores.

items.statement: Top 20 deposit concentration down to 6.61%; granularity improving alongside growth and cost reduction
items.quote: Our top 20 has gone down to 6.61%. So it's all the three. And many of you who have been on the presentations that we, that Ravi and I did, we said that it is not 2 out of 3, or 1 out of 3, it's all the 3 together, all the time.

items.statement: Headcount reduced from 11,339 to 10,981 YoY while growing advances 18.5% and deposits 19.5%; organic sourcing, vendor renegotiation, digitalization and AI driving efficiency
items.quote: Also, what is pertinent to note is that we have grown 18.5% in advances and 19.5% in deposits with less number of employees than we had in Q3 of last year. We had 11,339 people same time last year. We have 10,981 people now.

items.statement: One-time INR 26.87 cr labour code impact; incremental quarterly wage bill impact marginal (~INR 1 cr/quarter); cost-to-income 61.84% lower than Q3 FY25
items.quote: On the cost front, we have taken an impact of INR 26.87 crores on account of the new labour code. Despite this, our cost to income is at 61.84%, which is lower than Q3 of last year and cost to average assets is the same as of Q3 of last year. I want to clarify that the quarterly incremental impact of the wage bill would be marginal.

items.statement: Capital raise timeline- and event-based; no urgency now but will be needed for future growth; book value rising ~INR 5/quarter
items.quote: We have both as a timeline based as well as event based. We are pretty much clear of how much we want to take and at what rate we want to take it. So right now, there is no urgency for capital. But for future growth, we require it.

items.statement: Savings account rate at 1.5% floor limits further SA cost reduction benefit; future NIM expansion dependent on term deposit repricing and further repo cuts
items.quote: Currently, we're at 1.5% at the lowest end of the scale. So, when the same, the difference, honestly, between the delta of 16 bps and 10 bps is the impact of savings account cut. So one way of looking at it for the future is that you wil l get the benefit from TD going forward. There may not be too much benefit coming from a SA reduction. Unless there is more repo rate cut happening in the future.

items.statement: Operating profit grew 19% YoY; jaws widening with income growing 16% and expenses 15% including one-time labour cost
items.quote: The jaws are widening with income growing at 16% and expenses, including the onetime , growing at 15%. This has resulted in the operating profit growth of 19% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: RWA grew 5% QoQ, in line with 7% asset growth; well below 50% of assets
items.quote: The RWA movement is 5%, which is similar to the overall growth of the book. So it has grown in similar terms to the asset growth, the Q-o-Q asset growth. On a 7% asset growth, we have had an RWA increase of 5%.

items.statement: MD says bank will surpass all guidance given for FY26
items.quote: Whatever guidance we have given, we'll surpass that. There is no doubt in that.

items.statement: MD expects domestic NIM may dip 1-2 bps in Q4 FY26 due to MCLR repricing
items.quote: But this quarter may be 1 or 2 basis points NIM negative impact may come because MCLR book is repricing around 37% in this quarter.

items.statement: MD says credit cost will be maintained at current level, may rise 1-2 bps in Q4
items.quote: Credit cost, we'll maintain this level. I think we will be able to maintain. Although I have given guidance of less than 1, but I think at least next quarter, I will be able to maintain.

items.statement: MD targets gross NPA below 2% and net NPA at 0.5%
items.quote: I have already given guidance of less than 2%. We'll maintain that. Net NPA, 0.5%. We can do 0, but then after 0, what to do? So, we will maintain that.

items.statement: MD expects treasury income of around Rs 350 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: treasury, next quarter, I am expecting somewhere around R s 350 crore. So, there will be/ I am expecting some moderation in the treasury income

items.statement: MD says ECL implementation impact will be absorbed within one year, not five
items.quote: My endeavour will not definitely to take five years. So, first year itself, we will do whatever we have to do.

items.statement: MD targets digital business share to rise from 15% to 50% in 2-3 years
items.quote: My target is, say, my total digital business is 15%. I want to take it up to 50% in next two to three years.

items.statement: MD sets internal target to double total business to over Rs 25 lakh crore by Dec 2029
items.quote: December to January, I have internally set a target that we will double the business figure in five years December last December. So that means more than 25 lakh crore by Dec-2029.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline of around Rs 50,000 crore
items.quote: Last point, we have a good pipeline of around Rs 50,000 crore in the corporate credit.

items.statement: Nine-month sanctions at Rs 2.95 lakh crore, exceeding full FY25 sanctions of Rs 2.62 lakh crore
items.quote: sanction also , whatever it was sanctioned in the last financial year, R s 2.62 trillion. So far in these nine months, we have already sanctioned R s 2.95 lakh crore

items.statement: AUC recovery guidance of Rs 2,000 crore already achieved in nine months
items.quote: AUC recovery, we have guidance of R s 2,000 crore. We have already reached that figure R s 2,000 crore we have already reached

items.statement: NCLT recovery of Rs 338 crore in Q3 FY26
items.quote: NCLT recovery, one good account/ one chunky account has been recovered during this quarter. In that, around R s 300 crore recovery has come, so through recovery through NCLT is Rs 338 crore

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved sequentially from 3.34% to 3.40% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Domestic NIM has improved sequentially from 3.34% to 3.40%.

items.statement: Fresh slippages Rs 997 crore, recoveries Rs 1,453 crore in Q3; nine-month recovery Rs 5,153 crore vs guidance Rs 5,500-6,500 crore
items.value: slippages Rs 997 cr, recovery Rs 1,453 cr
items.quote: Fresh slippage during the quarter has been R s 997 crore, and recovery is R s 1,453 crore. If I talk of the nine-month recovery, nine-month recovery is approximately Rs 5,200 crore, to be precise Rs 5,153 crore, against a guidance of between Rs 5,500 crore to Rs 6,500 crore

items.statement: SMA book Rs 31,488 crore: SMA 0 Rs 12,000 cr, SMA 1 Rs 8,000 cr, SMA 2 Rs 11,000 cr; 10% provision on SMA 1 & 2
items.quote: Total SMA book is Rs 31,488 crore. Out of that, SMA 0 is Rs 12,000 crore, SMA 1 is Rs 8,000 crore, SMA 2 is almost Rs 11,000 crore. So, Rs 11,000 crore and Rs 8,000 crore, on Rs 19,000 crore, 10%.

items.statement: Additional Rs 380 crore provision made on SMA 1 in Q3, raising coverage from 5% to 10%
items.quote: Last quarter, I have made provision of 5% on SMA 1. This quarter, I have increased it up to 10%, so additional R s 380 crore provision we have made on SMA 1

items.statement: Two PSU accounts of Rs 3,000 crore moved to SMA 2 but have state government guarantee, low slip risk
items.quote: There are two PSU accounts where state government guarantee is available. So, last quarter, that was in SMA 0. This quarter, it has come to SMA 2. So, I mean, chances of slipping these account are, I mean, very less.

items.statement: IT capex plus opex around Rs 2,000 crore per annum for next 12-24 months
items.quote: Around Rs 2,000 crore per annum. Including both capex and opex. Because majority of IT expenditure is also coming in the shape of opex.

items.statement: Retired Rs 2,000 crore Tier 1 bonds, no fresh Tier 1 raised; CRAR 16.58%, CET1 14.54%
items.quote: Rs 2,000 crore of Tier 1 bond has retired, but we have not gone for raising fresh Tier 1, because we are still well capitalized. CET1 is 14.54%.

items.statement: Board approval for QIP up to Rs 5,000 crore kept as enabling clause, no immediate equity need
items.quote: Even this year, I have kept approval from the Board for QIP, up to Rs 5,000 crore. If you get opportunity, we can, of course. But as a part we don't need as of now.

items.statement: DICGC premium up Rs 128 crore (Rs 82 cr prior years, Rs 46 cr current quarter); Rs 60 cr ongoing quarterly increase
items.quote: they have also asked for the yesteryears. So DICGC cost itself has gone up by Rs 128 crore. Out of that, Rs 82 crore relates to previous years, remaining relate to this quarter, which will also be going forward, that will continue. Around Rs 60 crore increase in DICGC premium will continue

items.statement: Employee benefit expense up Rs 102 crore QoQ due to AS 15 actuarial valuation
items.quote: AS 15, we have made. If you see, from last quarter, it has gone up by Rs 102 crore. So that is purely based on the actuarial valuation.

items.statement: New labour code impact assessed at only Rs 55.86 lakh
items.quote: Yes, assessed, and we have impact of only Rs 56 lakhs. To be precise, Rs 55.86 lakhs.

items.statement: MD sees credit growth sustaining at 12-13% in FY27, cautious on aggressive growth to avoid risk build-up
items.quote: I think 12% to 13% growth is good, Darshil. Because see, if you pursue very aggressive growth no, then you will start asking why your NPA is going up.

items.statement: Green finance portfolio growing ~60%; strong demand in EV, solar, logistics/warehousing
items.quote: If you see, I give you just one number. My growth in green finance itself is around 60%. So, we have good pipeline of that also.

items.statement: Digital business Rs 1.98 lakh crore in Q3 (66% YoY); 169 fintech partners, 147 digital journeys, 94% digital transactions
items.quote: The Bank's digital business footprint is at R s 1.98 lakh crore for Q3, nine months ended FY26. That is a growth of 66% YoY and cumulative digital business has crossed Rs 4.52 lakh crore

items.statement: MSME digital app launched Feb 2025: 25k customers, 2.42 lakh logins, Rs 14,000+ cr financial transactions in Q3
items.quote: The best part is that our MSME app, which was launched last financial year in February '25, has a customer base of around 25,000, and the platform has a login of 2.42 lakhs and their financial transaction value is 14,000+ crore during this Q3.

items.statement: Export exposure only 4-5% to US; no material impact seen from tariffs/geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Tariff, yes, we have assessment. We are not seeing much impact. Our total export business is very minuscule. Exposure to US is only 4% to 5%. So, I am not seeing any much of the impact of that.

items.statement: No moratorium extended to MSMEs for export-related disruptions
items.quote: So far, we have not extended.

items.statement: RAM advances grew 16.65% YoY to Rs 3.90 trillion (Retail 18.54%, Agri 15.14%, MSME 16.41%)
items.quote: RAM grew by 16.65% and reached Rs 3.90 trillion. Retail grew by 18.54% and reached R s 1.36 trillion. Agriculture also grew by 15.14% and reached Rs 1.49 trillion. MSME grew by 16.41% and reached Rs 1.05 trillion

items.statement: MCLR-linked book 46.07%; 37% repricing due in Q4, 20% in Q1 FY27; deposit repricing 18% in Q4, 53% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: My MCLR-linked loan book is 46.07%, and out of that, repricing in this quarter is also due of around 37%, next quarter also, wherever quarterly reset or half-yearly reset is there, so that is 20%. Deposit also, repricing is due 18% in this quarter and 53% in next quarter.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment is stable and cautiously positive with consistent footfall growth; spending is occasion-driven rather than impulse-driven.
items.quote: We see consumer sentiment. If I describe it, it is stable and cautiously positive. I would not say too positive, but yes, cautiously, it is positive. It is not exuberant, definitely not fragile. We are seeing consistent footfall growth across markets.

items.statement: Tier 2, Tier 3 and rural markets show healthy growth supported by agriculture outcomes and shift to organized retail.
items.quote: Tier 2, Tier 3 market for us continues to be -- continues to show healthy returns or healthy growth. Rural or semi -urban consumer -- markets, the sentiment there has improved.

items.statement: Festive demand was reasonable; winter demand delayed but not lost, with erratic weather patterns affecting Eastern and Southern markets.
items.quote: So festive demand overall was reasonable. Diwali, which was n ot a winter -led Diwali, yet the demand was good, was okay. It was not great, but it was -- the demand held up. Winter demand definitely got delayed a little bit.

items.statement: Offline gross margins expanded 70 bps YoY due to better inventory health, less discounting, and improved product mix from marriage season.
items.quote: Importantly, excluding LimeRoad also, gross margins in the offline business actually expanded by 70 bps year -on-year, which was largely driven by better inventory health, leading to better efficiency which also necessitat ed lesser discounting intensity.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin improved from 10.8% to 12.2%; post-IndAS EBITDA grew 22% YoY to INR 210 crores with margins expanding 190 bps to 18.6%.
items.quote: As a net result of the sustained operational efficiencies, our pre IndAS EBITDA improved from 10.8% in last year to 12.2% this year. And the reported, which is the post Ind AS EBITDA grew 22% ye ar-on-year to INR 210 crores, with margins expanding by 190 bps to 18.6%.

items.statement: Full-year offline gross margins expected to remain broadly stable versus last year as value proposition focuses on volume-led growth.
items.quote: And for the full year also, we expect the offline gross margins to remain broadly stable versus last year as our value proposition continues to focus on volume-led growth.

items.statement: Capex for Q3 was INR 57 crores primarily for new store additions and selective refurbishments.
items.quote: Capex for the quarter stood at INR 57 crores, primarily towards new store additions and selective refurbishments.

items.statement: Targeting 75-plus new store additions for FY26 as communicated in last quarter's call.
items.quote: As communicated in last quarter's call, we are looking to end the year with 75 -plus new stores additions this year.

items.statement: Added 23 new stores in Q3, taking total store count to 554; new stores ramping up faster than historical averages.
items.quote: We continue to execute well on our expansion strategy, adding 23 new stores during the quarter, taking the total store count to 554 stores.

items.statement: Long-term target of 13-14% annual square footage addition; 60-65% of expansion from new towns in existing states.
items.quote: The square footage addition on an annual basis should be at around 13%, 14%. That is what we have targeted. And that is a long -term target that we have taken.

items.statement: Winter assortment mix was 40-45% for the quarter, rising to 62-63% in December; balance 55-58% from basic and autumn products.
items.quote: Our winter is normally -- this quarter are upwards of 40% mix, the winter, pre-winter what we categorize. If we go towards the December, the peak winter season, it goes up to 62%, 63% also. But at an overall level, including the festive month, it was around 40%, 45%.

items.statement: Private labels now almost 70% of assortment, blended with market labels to suit regional tastes via deep vendor network.
items.quote: this is the strengt h of V-Mart is, we definitely blend both our private labels, which is almost 70% now, and the market labels, which to suit our -- the regional requirement or the local taste of the consumer

items.statement: Inventory days increased marginally by 1% to 95 days due to strategic FMCG space increase for winter apparel; inventory freshness improved YoY.
items.quote: Our days of inventory increased marginally by 1% to 95 days. This slight increase is largely due to the slight change in the FMCG inventory, as we strategically increased space for apparel offtake during winter.

items.statement: Expansions fully funded by internal accruals; balance sheet strong and virtually debt-free.
items.quote: Our expansions have been completely funded by our internal accruals, keeping the balance sheet strong and virtually debt -free.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth normalized at stable 5-6%; medium to long-term aspiration of 5-8% mid-to-high single digit.
items.quote: The SSG aspirations always need to be mid - to high single digit, 5% to 8%. So t hat's the aspiration.

items.statement: Unlimited new stores delivering sales per sq ft and profitability in line with V-Mart model; target to bring full Unlimited network to V-Mart average in 2-3 years.
items.quote: And as the average of these new stores starts to take over the average of the legacy stores, we will see improved sales per square feet numbers also for the complete Unlimited chain.

items.statement: Input costs easing providing margin support; vigilant on reversals or one-time expense rises.
items.quote: Definitely, our input costs are getting eased, which do provide margin support. But yes, we are very vigilant on any of these reversals or any onetime expense rise.

items.statement: Recognized exceptional cost of INR 2.1 crores for proposed labour code changes; rules not yet announced.
items.quote: On the labour code impact, we recognized an exceptional cost of INR 2 crores, INR2.1 crores arising out of the changes proposed. While the rules are yet to be announced, but basis, whatever information and the guidance available was there, we have taken a onetime hit as prescribed by law.

items.statement: Driving more sales per employee through technology integration, process reduction, and digital marketing; focusing on Google ratings and NPS for customer experience.
items.quote: we are trying to drive more sales out of the same number of people or less number of people. We're trying to drive more sales by reducing some processes, by integrating technology, by bringing in some additional new ways of marketing

items.statement: Competition increasing in value retail, expanding awareness and footfall for organized retail as a whole.
items.quote: In our market, competition has also increased, definitely giving more choices to consumers. Importantly, this is increasing the -- or expanding the awareness and the footfall for organized retail as a whole.

items.statement: Weather disruptions (excess rainfall, cyclones, delayed winter) and geopolitical uncertainty affecting urban consumer sentiment.
items.quote: We have seen excess rainfall or activity of cyclones during festivals, in parts of Eastern India, in southern markets. So we have seen some disruption on these market s and some lower growth also coming in here.

items.statement: YTD PAT grown almost 3x to INR 113 crores reflecting consistency; positive free cash flow of INR 63 crores, up 9.4% YoY.
items.quote: On a full year basis or rather on a YTD basis, PAT has now grown almost 3x to INR113 crores, reflecting consistency rather than quarter -specific efforts. Coming to inventory. Our days of inventory increased marginally by 1% to 95 days.

items.statement: Rental per sq ft: V-Mart ~INR 48-49, Unlimited ~INR 65; rental cost as % of sales to decline as SSG grows.
items.quote: V- Mart should be closer to around INR 48, INR49. And for Unlimited, that would be at around INR65.

items.statement: Expect ADTO to remain at current levels with plus/minus 5% variation going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we continue to believe that our ADTO numbers should remain in the similar numbers with plus/minus 5% kind of a variation going forward.

items.statement: Target to double MTF book from Rs 450-odd crores to Rs 900-1,000 crores in next two years
items.quote: Next two-year target is to double the book from Rs. 450-odd crores to anywhere between Rs. 900 crores to, four figures, to Rs. 1,000 crores is our aim.

items.statement: Expect Silverleaf merger to add Rs 50-60 crores gross revenue initially, potentially 2x-3x in 1-2 years
items.quote: Silverleaf, once the merger will be done , we are expecting top line of Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60-odd crores, and that's the initial revenues. And we are very hopeful the kind of technology they are bringing in, going further, if a parent Company like Share India is there, and we just help with mor e risk appetite and more capital exposure to them, then these numbers can easily multiply by 2x to 3x

items.statement: Expect uTrade revenue to multiply 2x-3x in next 1-2 years as it opens to multi-broker distribution
items.quote: And we believe that uTrade numbers should also multiply by 2 x to 3x in next one or two years

items.statement: Expect insurance business to grow 20-25% year-on-year for full year FY26
items.quote: So, full year projection, we are expecting at least 20% to 25% growth year-on-year basis from April to March.

items.statement: Market participation improving with volumes growing after stabilization period
items.quote: Market participation is also improving. Slowly volumes have started going up now. And we think that we have crossed the worst period and not up, but at least stabilization, we can definitely see.

items.statement: Commodity trading volumes increased due to volatility in gold and silver prices
items.quote: Commodity market, especially in the last quarter has seen a really uptick, which we believe is a structural number and should continue at those similar levels.

items.statement: NBFC NIMs to decline a few hundred basis points further as secured book mix increases to 40%
items.quote: And as the industry practice is, in secured book there is a comparatively lower amount of NIMs that we maintain. So, the blended NIMs that you would see, we will see a few more hundred basis points dow nward traction before they stabilize at that level

items.statement: MTF book increased 3% quarter-to-quarter from Rs 443 crores to Rs 457 crores despite volatile market
items.quote: MTF book has increased marginally by 3% quarter-to-quarter. It was Rs. 443 crores in Quarter 2, which have gone up to Rs. 457 crores.

items.statement: ADTO jumped 29% quarter-to-quarter from Rs 7,500 crores to Rs 9,700 crores
items.quote: ADTO, average daily turnover, has gone up from Rs. 7,500 crores in Quarter 2 to Rs. 9,700 crores in Quarter 3. That's really a big jump, Rs. 2,200 crores, ADTO's jump from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3.

items.statement: Active retail equity clients increased 1% quarter-to-quarter despite dormant account closures
items.quote: We have seen an 1% increase in the number of active clients in Share India overall equities from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3.

items.statement: Active institutional clients grew 13% quarter-to-quarter from 154 to 174
items.quote: So, we have seen a 13% growth in active clients in the institutional side from 154 to 174, it's a growth of 20.

items.statement: Wealth management, PMS, AIF, and debt distribution platform to launch from Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, next year you will see a lot of new initiatives will start showing some ground like AIF, PMS, wealth distribution and Share India Cred Capital also will be operational from the next financial year.

items.statement: Silverleaf merger expected to complete by end of Q4 FY26, adding professionally trained traders
items.quote: So, they are in advanced stage, so we believe NCLT approval should come by end of this quarter. So, Silverleaf merger will happen next financial year, that will also add to the numbers of the Share India in next financial year.

items.statement: Plan to open five pilot branches in Tier-3 cities from April 2026 (Q1 FY27)
items.quote: So, from April onwards we will start all these branches at five different locations, again, Q1 next financial year.

items.statement: NBFC NPAs increased in Q3 due to unsecured book stress but expected to trend downward as secured book grows
items.quote: But going forward, we should see these kind of NPAs going downward only. Plus as our secured book grow, the blended NPAs will go further down from those levels.

items.statement: NBFC unsecured book reduced to ~Rs 100 crores out of Rs 250 crores total book
items.quote: Of the Rs. 250-odd crores book that we have currently left, around Rs. 100 crores is only present in the unsecured nature.

items.statement: Merchant banking focusing on main board IPOs over SME due to lower cyclicity; one main board IPO filed in September, another in January
items.quote: We have filed one main board IPO in September, which we are awaiting approval, which we should hopefully open in next quarter. We have also filed one more main board IPO in January this year.

items.statement: Consolidated operating profit margin at 43% and net profit margin at 24%
items.quote: Operating profit margin stands at 43% and net profit margin at 24%.

items.statement: Consolidated debt-equity ratio comfortable at 0.24% and current ratio at 2.12x
items.quote: Debt equity ratio is comfortable at 0.24%. Current ratio is at 2.12x.

items.statement: Declared third interim dividend of Rs 0.40 per share (20% on face value of Rs 2)
items.quote: We have also declared a third interim dividend of Rs. 0.40 per share, that comes to around 20% on the face value.

items.statement: Silverleaf merger in advanced NCLT stage, expected to complete next financial year
items.quote: So, they are in advanced stage, so we believe NCLT approval should come by end of this quarter. So, Silverleaf merger will happen next financial year.

items.statement: Formed Share India Cred Capital Private Limited (incorporated 6 Jan 2026) for tech-driven fixed income distribution
items.quote: Company is called Shar e India Cred Capital Private Limited. It is a subsidiary of the Share India Securities. This Company has been incorporated on 6th January 2026

items.statement: Formed Share India Wealth Multiplier Solutions Private Limited as wholly owned subsidiary for AIF license
items.quote: AIF, we have applied for the license and the new Company formed called Share India Wealth Multiplier Solutions Private Limited. So, a new AIF license, it actually has been applied in Share India Wealth Multiplier Solutions Private Limited. This Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Share India.

items.statement: Wealth management recruitment underway with mid-sized managers appointed, execution plan ready for Q1 FY27 launch
items.quote: Recruitment is still in place, still some fairly midsized managers have been appointed and execution plan is on the table now. So, I believe from the Q1 of next financial year, we will see that the wealth management team will be on the ground.

items.statement: Short-term risks include global trade tensions, FII outflows, muted IPO activity, and inflation potentially delaying rate cuts
items.quote: Short-term range -bound trading purchase due to global trade tensions, FI I outflow and muted IPO activity, inflation edging up may delay further rate cuts, capping upside for the near term

items.statement: Strategy differs from Groww/Zerodha by focusing on physical presence in Tier-3 cities and high-touch multi-product distribution rather than mass digital acquisition
items.quote: Comparing a Company like Share India directly with likes of Groww or Zerodha would be a very unfair assessment. We are more of a physical presence, brick-and-mortar kind of a player. Our strategy is more on the lines, as sir has explained already, in offering multiple products with high touch base

items.statement: Gross margin guidance of 32% to 34% for the quarter
items.quote: Gross margin was at 29.8%, approximately 30%, slightly below our guidance of 32% to 34%, primarily due to elevated commodity prices, especially copper during the quarter.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin remained stable at 7.5% in Q3 FY26

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Targets 25% AUM growth for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: As we move toward FY27, we are positioned to achieve 25% AUM growth driven by enhanced distribution , technology adoption supported by diversified funding and robust risk management.

items.statement: Targets 25% AUM growth for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: The target is to end the year at 25% AUM growth. And again, for the next year, we have given the guidance of 25% growth on AUM.

items.quote: In this quarter, we added two branches, with the latest additions comprising one in Karnataka and one in Madhya Pradesh. We have 6-8 branches in the pipeline and at least 6 branches will be added in Q4.

items.quote: FY27, again, we are looking to add about 25 -30 branches. It will again follow the same path where we are concentrating. MP will be one of the states. Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, these would be frontrunners next year in terms of branch additions.

items.quote: Monthly disbursements crossed Rs. 500 crores for the first time in December 2025.

Co-lending would continue to be an important part of our strategy to strengthen our ability to cater to higher ticket size segments. We aim to take co-lending contribution to 10% of AUM as we scale.

items.quote: Net interest margin for the quarter was at 6.0 %, up from 5.4% in the previous quarter, supported by gearing, optimized liquidity position and lower cost of borrowing.

items.quote: Yes, effective from 1st Jan, we have reduced our PLR by 10 bps. And we have passed on that benefit to customers from 1st of January.

items.quote: With proactive management, we were able to contract our cos t of borrowing ex -co-lending by 10 bps at 8%, supporting our ex-co-lending spread of 5.4%.

items.statement: Expect 5-10 bps borrowing cost reduction per quarter for next 2-3 quarters; no further PLR cut in Q4
items.quote: Moving forward, we should expect a little bit of maybe 5 -10 bps every quarter for t he next 2-3 quarters. And basis that we will have to go back to see how the rates are looking like, what we are getting and eventually look at the PLR. I would think that we will not do any more PLR reduction in this quarter, which is Q4 of this year. Anything from here on will be next year only.
